title: ASSEMBLER
description:
About Company:

Our History

Since our humble beginning as a small blacksmith shop in 1882, Brunner & Lay has grown to include manufacturing plants and warehouses on three different continents. These include seven facilities in the United States, two in Canada, three in Great Britain, one in Germany, and two in Australia. We have played a role in the construction of some of the world’s most famous highways, dams, airfields, mines, quarries, and even national monuments.


American Made since 1882

About the Role:

The Assembler plays a critical role in the manufacturing process by accurately and efficiently assembling components into finished products according to detailed specifications. This position ensures that all parts are correctly fitted, secured, and inspected to meet quality standards, contributing directly to the overall production output and customer satisfaction. The Assembler works closely with production teams to maintain a smooth workflow on the assembly line, adhering to safety protocols and operational guidelines. Attention to detail and manual dexterity are essential to identify and resolve any assembly issues promptly, minimizing downtime and defects. Ultimately, the Assembler helps uphold the company’s reputation for delivering reliable, high-quality products within scheduled timelines.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Experience with assembly processes in a manufacturing environment.
  • Proficiency in using hand tools and power equipment such as drill presses and band saws.
  • Ability to read and interpret assembly instructions, blueprints, and technical documents.
  • Strong attention to detail and manual dexterity.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience working on a production or assembly line.
  • Basic soldering skills.
  • Familiarity with quality control and visual inspection techniques.
  • Knowledge of safety standards and best practices in manufacturing.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and meet production targets.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform assembly of components using hand tools, power equipment, and machinery such as drill presses and band saws according to work orders and blueprints.
  • Operate and maintain production line equipment to ensure continuous and efficient assembly operations.
  • Conduct visual inspections of assembled products to verify quality and adherence to specifications.
  • Follow safety procedures and maintain a clean and organized work area to promote a safe manufacturing environment.
  • Collaborate with team members and supervisors to troubleshoot assembly issues and implement process improvements.

Skills:

The required skills such as assembly process knowledge, hand tool proficiency, and operation of power equipment are essential for performing precise and efficient assembly tasks daily. Soldering and drill press operation skills enable the assembler to handle specialized assembly steps that require technical expertise. Visual inspection skills are used continuously to ensure that each product meets quality standards before moving to the next stage of production. Familiarity with the production and assembly line environment helps the assembler maintain workflow and collaborate effectively with team members. Preferred skills like quality control understanding and safety awareness further enhance the assembler’s ability to contribute to a safe, high-quality manufacturing process.

title: Senior Solution Architect
description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Solution Architect to join our growing Enterprise Architecture team at a pivotal moment of build-out. The successful candidate will lead the design and delivery of fit-for-purpose solutions across our technology estate, working within the patterns, standards, and reference architectures set by our Domain Architects, and translating those into tangible architectural outputs that support both internal business operations and the development of commercially valuable solutions for our clients and market offerings.

This role requires a proven strategic leader who can bridge the gap between technical requirements and business objectives whilst influencing senior stakeholders across the organisation. You will work collaboratively with our delivery teams, including Software Engineering, Infrastructure, Commercial Technology, and Corporate Technology, to guide implementation, ensure architectural consistency, and embed best practises throughout the product development lifecycle. You will also mentor and coach junior members of the architecture team, fostering their professional development and technical excellence. The ideal candidate will balance the organisation's risk appetite with operational excellence, translating complex requirements into practical, scalable solutions that enable the business.

Job Functions

  • Lead the design of complex solution architectures for Colliers' systems and products, partnering closely with engineering and platform teams throughout delivery to ensure architectural intent is maintained and applicable standards and policies are upheld.

  • Author and maintain core solution architecture artefacts, including Preliminary Architecture Blueprints, Solution Design Documents, and Architecture Decision Records, to a standard that enables engineering, security, and governance teams to act on them confidently and with minimal rework.

  • Engage with senior stakeholders across Software Engineering, Infrastructure, Commercial Technology, Corporate Technology, and business leadership to ensure that architectural principles are embedded throughout the product delivery lifecycle and aligned with strategic objectives.

  • Apply and compose solutions using the cloud reference architectures, patterns, and standards maintained by our Domain Architects, spanning Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform, alongside other surface areas including application architecture, data, and integration.

  • Lead architectural reviews and assessments, identifying technical risks, and recommending mitigation strategies that align with business objectives whilst providing authoritative guidance on complex technical decisions.

  • Mentor and coach junior Solution Architects and technical staff, developing their architectural thinking, design skills, and understanding of enterprise architecture principles and practises.

  • Provide strategic guidance and advisory support to delivery teams on engaging with the Enterprise Architecture function, helping them navigate architectural governance processes, design review procedures, and organisational policies to ensure timely and effective collaboration.

  • Lead engagement with senior business stakeholders to understand strategic objectives, translate business vision into technical strategy, and articulate the value and trade-offs of architectural decisions.

  • Analyse complex technical requirements and constraints across application, data, integration, and cloud domains, developing innovative solution designs that address scalability, performance, resilience, security, and cost optimisation whilst balancing competing priorities.

  • stay current with developments and emerging technologies and delivery patterns across all relevant domains, leading proof-of-concept initiatives and making strategic recommendations for adoption that align with the organisation's technical roadmap.

  • Lead responses to audits, technical due diligence, and architecture assessments from internal and external stakeholders, representing the organisation's architectural capability and maturity.

  • Contribute to the development of the Enterprise Architecture function itself, improving processes, governance frameworks, and collaborative practises.

  • Act as an embedded architect within product and delivery squads, providing continuous design partnership across discovery, delivery, and run phases, whilst maintaining a strong connection to the global Enterprise Architecture practice and its standards.

  • Leverage AI-augmented tooling responsibly to accelerate solution design, decision documentation, and review preparation, in line with Colliers' approved AI usage policies and standards.

  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent demonstrable industry experience.

  • Professional cloud architecture certifications including Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert and Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect.

  • Demonstrated track record of delivering architecture across multiple domain areas, with relevant certifications across areas such as cloud platforms, cyber security, data management, integration technologies, or software development considered advantageous. Enterprise architecture certifications such as TOGAF are beneficial but not a prerequisite.

  • Demonstrated track record of leading the architecture of multiple non-trivial systems end-to-end, including at least one greenfield and one brownfield engagement at enterprise scale, with evidence of decisions documented and outcomes measured.

  • Extensive experience designing and guiding the delivery of large-scale solutions on Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform in enterprise or commercial environments, with proven multi-cloud expertise.

  • Familiarity with the commercial real estate technology landscape, including property management systems, valuation platforms, capital markets technology, and workplace or IWMS platforms, is a strong plus.

  • Experience operating as an embedded architect inside product teams within an organisation transitioning to a product-based operating model is highly desirable.

  • Deep technical knowledge of cloud-native services including compute (VMs, containers, serverless), storage, networking (VNets, VPCs, hybrid connectivity), databases, and integration patterns, with the ability to make strategic technology decisions.

  • Strong experience with infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps practises, and modern software delivery methodologies.

  • Proven expertise in multi-cloud and hybrid cloud architectures, including cloud migration strategies, patterns, and hands-on delivery experience.

  • Deep understanding and practical application of architectural frameworks and methodologies such as TOGAF, or similar enterprise architecture approaches. Equally important is fluency with the modern architecture toolkit, including C4 modelling, Architecture Decision Records, value stream and capability mapping, event storming, Domain-Driven Design, fitness functions, evolutionary architecture principles, and Team Topologies, alongside the judgement to apply the right technique to the problem at hand.

  • Expert knowledge of non-functional requirements including scalability, performance, resilience, disaster recovery, and security by design, with experience making architectural trade-offs.

  • Strong experience with solution costing, TCO analysis, business case development, and commercial considerations in cloud solution design.

  • Extensive technical knowledge across multiple domains including application architecture, data architecture, integration patterns, API design, microservices, event-driven architectures, and cloud networking.

  • Strong familiarity with common IT frameworks such as ITIL, and deep awareness of governance, risk, and compliance requirements in enterprise environments.

  • Demonstrated experience mentoring, coaching, and developing junior technical staff and architects.

  • Proven ability to engage with and influence senior stakeholders, C-level executives, and business leaders, articulating complex technical concepts in business terms.

  • Excellent presentation and communication skills, with experience presenting architectural proposals and strategies to diverse audiences.

  • Fluent spoken and written English is essential for effective communication with global teams, senior stakeholders, and for producing architectural documentation and technical guidance materials. Fluency in Spanish is desirable, given the role is based in our Madrid tech centre and will involve day-to-day collaboration with local colleagues and stakeholders.

If you enjoy working in a positive, energetic, and dynamic work environment that emphasises social as well as business interaction, then we invite you to apply.

title: Export Coordinator
description:
Export Coordinator

Location: Heler Foods Creamery, Nantwich
Salary: £30,000 – £34,000
Contract: Full time | Fixed-term (6 – 9 months)

Heler Foods Creamery, Nantwich – our original farmhouse home, where traditional British cheesemaking and innovation come together.

At Heler Foods, our people are part of our extended Heler Family — the driving force behind everything we do. From crafting award-winning cheeses to delivering service that sets new standards, we work together to shape the future of food.

CHEESEMAKERS. FUTURE SHAPERS. CHANGEMAKERS.

Rooted in tradition and growing into the future, we’re bold, ambitious and proud of where we’re going next.

Every colleague has a voice here — and every step you take helps move us forward.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We’re looking for an Export Coordinator to join our Trading team at our Nantwich site.

Working as part of the Trading team, you will provide key administrative and coordination support to ensure the smooth processing of export orders from start to finish. You will be responsible for managing export documentation, maintaining accurate records, coordinating communications and supporting internal teams, customers and external partners to ensure orders are delivered efficiently.

This is a full-time role fixed term, working 5 days per week.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Providing administrative support to the Trading team by coordinating and maintaining all required export documentation and paperwork.
  • Managing export order administration, ensuring information is accurate, complete and communicated within required timescales.
  • Compiling customer shipping documentation and organising veterinary checks as required.
  • Liaising with Veterinary Surgeons to ensure export documentation is completed accurately, including changes to destination legislation and requirements.
  • Ensuring all export orders processed through Heler Foods’ European entity are accurately logged and communicated to the Operations team.
  • Acting as a key point of contact for export customers, ensuring all required information and updates are provided in a timely and professional manner.
  • Maintaining export records, sales trackers and spreadsheets to support reporting, forecasting and order visibility.
  • Supporting the wider Trading team with day-to-day administration and coordination activities to ensure customer requirements are met.

ABOUT YOU

We’re looking for someone who is organised, proactive and enjoys working in a fast-paced environment. You will have excellent attention to detail, strong communication skills and the ability to coordinate multiple activities to support our Trading team and export customers.

Essential:

  • Experience within an administration, coordination, customer service, trading support, sales support or commercial environment.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Excellent attention to detail, particularly when managing documentation, data and customer information.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to build positive relationships with internal teams, customers and external partners.
  • The ability to liaise effectively with internal departments including Production, Logistics, Supply Chain and Customer Service to manage orders from start to finish.
  • Confidence communicating with external stakeholders including customers, hauliers, customs partners and suppliers.
  • The ability to maintain accurate records, update spreadsheets and provide regular reporting information.
  • Strong computer skills, including confidence using Microsoft Word, Excel and spreadsheets.
  • The ability to work under pressure and manage competing priorities in a busy environment.

Desirable:

  • Previous experience within a food shipping, export or logistics environment.
  • Experience compiling customer shipping documentation and coordinating export requirements, including veterinary checks.
  • Experience processing and maintaining export shipments and documentation in line with regulations and company standards.
  • Experience coordinating samples with internal teams and arranging courier/transport requirements.
  • Experience raising purchase orders and supporting invoicing processes.
  • Experience supporting product set-up activities and customer sample processes.
  • Experience working closely with Production and Material Planning teams to ensure orders are achievable and delivered on time.
  • Experience monitoring export order activity, including weekly and monthly volumes.

You’ll also demonstrate behaviours aligned to our values:

Be Better | Be Collaborative | Be Inquisitive | Be Yourself | Take Ownership

We help our people become the best versions of themselves, take pride in what they do and bring out the strength in others. If that excites you — you’ll fit right in here.

title: Quality Control Inspector II
description:
Quality Control Inspector II

Department: Quality Control

Reports To: Quality Supervisor

Location: On-Site – Clinton, MD

Travel: Negligible

FLSA: Hourly, Full-Time, Non-Exempt

Revision Date: February 2025

About Vitesse: How we communicate, capture, and share information has not changed significantly in our lifetime—it has changed significantly in the last decade, even in the last year. From a vacationer checking email as they fly across the world to a U.S. military service member sharing critical observations across the battlefield, the ability to capture and transfer data over different platforms is an important part both of our everyday lives and the security of our country. Whether on a geostationary satellite, a naval vessel, or a military jet, the mission-critical solutions that we design and manufacture at Vitesse make our country and our world safer.

Through extensive technical expertise, Vitesse Systems optimizes the functionality of antenna and thermal management systems for the advancement of next-generation Radar, Electronic Warfare, and C4I (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence) systems.

Vitesse Systems prides itself on the solutions we provide to our customers, as well as the incredible team of dedicated people we employ.

SUMMARY: The Quality Control Inspector II is an intermediate level mechanical inspector role. The primary function of the role is to inspect components and assemblies for dimensional, aesthetic and workmanship characteristics. Simultaneously, the Quality Control Inspector II will verify documentation is complete and accurate from internal and external suppliers. This Team Member will perform all mechanical inspection using micrometers, calipers height gages and hardness testing equipment and will log data as required. The Quality Control Inspector II will interpret measuring results passing confirming product and will generate non-conformance documentation. Commitment to and support of the Company Core Values are key to success in this position.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform all work in manner that is safe for you and fellow team members and is compliant with Vitesse System safety policies.
  • Follow all quality procedures, work instructions, and documents pertaining to your job and department.
  • Complete all paperwork and documentation required with order.
  • Verify all traveler sign-offs, SPC sheets have been completed and signed off in accordance with good documentation practices.
  • Verify part number, revision, expiration dates and other data fields on supplier certification match work order or purchase order requirements.
  • Clock in/out to job operation promptly after assignment/completion recording quantity completed.
  • Inspect parts to blueprint specifications and workmanship standards.
  • Verify that all company and personal inspection equipment and tools being used are in calibration.
  • Report non-conformances to Quality Supervisor and Generate Non-Conformance reports for all discrepant material.
  • Identify potential issues/problems and contribute to corrective action investigations.
  • Independently operate equipment & tasks within allotted times.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Proficient in inspection tooling: height gages, calipers, micrometers, and hardness testing.
  • Proficient with setup and operation of CMM.
  • Inspection reports as required.
  • Proficient knowledge of basic Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Perform all functions of the job while adhering to established quality policies and procedures.
  • Uphold the company’s core values.
  • Other duties as assigned.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

QUALIFICATIONS:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Successful accomplishment of duties and responsibilities may require the following:

  • Must have the knowledge and experience necessary for the position.
  • Must be able to operate the various machines within the department with minimal instruction.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Must be capable of reading and understanding drawings, blueprints and specifications.
  • Must be able to inspect the parts they are machining.
  • Ability to measure with vernier caliper, micrometers and height gauges.
  • Must be able to follow instructions and procedures and work with minimal supervision.
  • Strong communication, both written and oral and problem-solving skills.
  • Must be adaptable to a changing work environment and competing demands.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills.


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

  • Actively supports and complies with Vitesse Systems objectives, guidelines and commitment to Quality and Safety, with an emphasis on continual improvement, transparency, and collaboration.
  • Must be able to interact effectively and cooperatively with Team Members at all levels.
  • Must have the ability to complete assignments within the timeframe specified by the Manager.
  • Must be flexible regarding working hours and overtime. Must be able to work overtime in the evenings and weekends, with or without advanced notice.
  • Must be able to operate in a fast-paced environment and handle multiple projects simultaneously.


EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:

  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED)
  • 2-4 year related experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience in an AS9100 environment preferred.


LANGUAGE SKILLS: Ability to speak and understand basic safety and manufacturing instructions.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS: Ability to add and subtract two-digit numbers. Ability to multiply and divide with 10’s and 100’s.

REASONING ABILITY: Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out detailed but uninvolved written or oral instructions. Ability to deal with problems involving a few concrete variables in standardized situations.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS: Authorization to work in the United States. To conform to U.S. export control regulations, you should be eligible for any required authorizations from the U.S. Government.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a Team Member to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the Team Member is regularly required to stand, walk, and hear. The Team Member frequently is required to use hands and fingers; handle, feel, and reach with hands and arms. The Team Member is occasionally required to sit; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and smell. The Team Member must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work environments characteristics described here are representative of those a Team Member encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this position, the Team Member is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The Team Member may be exposed to a hot and/or cold work environment, chemicals, fumes or airborne particles, loud noises, risk of electrical shock and vibration and/or other occupational hazards; personal protective equipment may be required.

NOTE: This job description identifies the general nature and scope of work to be performed. Vitesse Systems, LLC. reserves the right to revise all or any part of this job description and to add or eliminate essential job functions at any time. Designation of any job duty as an essential function is not intended as an assurance or guarantee that a team member has any right to perform the particular job duty, except as required by Vitesse Systems, LLC. This job description is subject to change based on the needs of the position and/or the Company.


Vitesse Systems, LLC performs work controlled by the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR). These statutes require the protection of technical data and products. The regulations require that such data not be disclosed in written, oral, or visual form to any foreign national without prior export authorization from the Department of State. A foreign national is defined by the U.S. Government under EAR 734.2(b)(2)(ii) and 8 USC 110 (a)(20) as one who:

  • Is not a United States citizen
  • Is not lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the U.S.
  • Does not have politically protected status (embassy, refugee, or asylum)
  • Has dual U.S. / foreign citizenship

title: Technical Sales Engineer
description:
Job title: Technical Sales Engineer

Reports to: VP, Priority Commerce - Revenue Management

Department: Central Services

Location: Remote

Grade: 20



About Priority:


Priority Commerce is a leading financial technology company on a mission to deliver a personalized, easy-to-adopt financial toolset that accelerates cash flow and optimizes working capital for businesses. Our vision is to eliminate the barriers to unlocking revenue - empowering businesses to grow faster and operate smarter.


We achieve this through the Priority Commerce Engine, an innovative platform that combines payables, acquiring, and banking and treasury solutions. This unified approach allows businesses to streamline financial operations, reduce unnecessary costs, and uncover new revenue opportunities.


At Priority Commerce, we're driven by results. We expect our people to be known for results - bringing expertise, momentum, and relentless focus to every challenge, helping our clients and each other thrive.



About the Role:

The Technical Sales Engineer serves as a customer-facing technical resource who partners with Sales throughout the pre-sales process to help prospects understand how Priority's products and technology can support their business needs. This role combines technical expertise with strong commercial awareness, translating complex product capabilities, APIs, and integration requirements into clear, practical solutions for prospective customers and partners.

The Technical Sales Engineer leads technical discovery, recommends optimal integration paths, responds to technical and API-related questions during the prequalification process, and delivers compelling product demonstrations tailored to the prospect's use case. The role helps identify technical considerations early in the sales process, reduce uncertainty, and provide prospects with confidence in Priority's ability to meet their needs.

Unlike Solution Architects, who are responsible for designing and supporting custom or complex integration builds, the Technical Solutions Support focuses on pre-sales technical consultation using established product capabilities and integration patterns, escalating opportunities requiring custom architecture or development to the appropriate technical teams.


Responsibilities:

  • Partner with Sales during the pre-sales process to understand prospect requirements, business workflows, technical environments, and integration needs.

  • Lead technical discovery conversations and recommend the most appropriate Priority products, APIs, integration methods, and established solution paths based on the prospect's requirements.

  • Serve as a technical subject-matter resource during prospect meetings, responding to questions related to APIs, integrations, product functionality, data flows, technical requirements, and platform capabilities.

  • Prepare and deliver engaging product demonstrations that connect Priority's capabilities to the prospect's business needs and clearly communicate the value of the proposed solution.

  • Translate complex technical concepts into clear, business-oriented language for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Assess technical feasibility during the sales process, identifying potential integration considerations, dependencies, limitations, or risks before commitments are made.

  • Clearly identify when an opportunity requires custom development or solution architecture and facilitate an effective handoff to Solution Architects, Product, or other technical teams.

  • Partner with Product and technical teams to maintain current knowledge of platform capabilities, APIs, integration options, product enhancements, and roadmap developments.

  • Develop and maintain reusable technical sales resources such as demonstration environments, integration diagrams, API guidance, technical FAQs, and discovery materials.

  • Capture recurring prospect requirements, technical objections, and integration needs and provide feedback to Product and Sales leadership to improve product positioning and the overall sales process.

  • Support Sales in communicating technically accurate solution approaches in proposals, presentations, and other customer-facing materials.


What Success Looks Like:

  • Sales teams have a trusted technical partner who can confidently lead technical conversations throughout the evaluation process.

  • Prospects receive clear, accurate guidance on how Priority's products will integrate with their technology and business processes.

  • Technical requirements, dependencies, and potential integration challenges are identified early, reducing downstream surprises during implementation.

  • Product demonstrations are tailored, engaging, and effectively connect Priority's technical capabilities to the prospect's business objectives.

  • Standard integration opportunities progress efficiently without unnecessary reliance on Solution Architects or Product teams.

  • Opportunities requiring custom architecture are identified early and transitioned to the appropriate technical resources with clear requirements and context.

  • Technical questions and objections are addressed quickly and accurately, helping Sales maintain momentum and accelerate opportunities through the pipeline.

  • Feedback from prospect conversations improves technical sales materials, product positioning, and Priority's understanding of emerging customer integration needs.


Candidate Requirements:


  • 4+ years of experience in sales engineering, solutions consulting, technical consulting, implementation, integrations, or a similar customer-facing technical role.

  • Experience supporting a B2B software, SaaS, payments, fintech, financial services, or other technology-driven sales organization.

  • Strong working knowledge of APIs, including REST APIs, authentication methods, webhooks, data structures, and common system integration concepts.

  • Ability to understand customer technical environments and translate business requirements into practical integration approaches.

  • Experience conducting technical discovery sessions and delivering customer-facing product demonstrations.

  • Strong presentation and communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and business audiences.

  • Commercial mindset with the ability to balance technical accuracy with the objectives and pace of the sales process.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and judgment regarding when an opportunity can be supported through standard capabilities versus when additional technical architecture is required.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively across Sales, Product, Engineering, Solution Architecture, Implementation, and Operations.

  • Ability to manage multiple opportunities and technical evaluations simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.



Work Environment & Culture:

We believe that performance and experience go hand in hand - an exceptional employee experience is earned through contribution. We are a results-driven team, grounded in our core values: ownership, authenticity, service, trust, innovation, and camaraderie.

Our culture is built for those who want to make an impact. We challenge each other to grow, celebrate progress, and support one another through shared goals and real connection. Whether you're building technology, serving clients, or supporting internal teams, you’ll be part of a company that empowers you to perform at your best and be known for results.


Compensation and Benefits:


Compensation range: $125k-$158k
We invest in the whole employee - personally and professionally. Our benefits package is designed to support your well-being, growth, and success - both inside and outside of work.


Financial Wellness

  • Bonus programs

  • 401(k) match

  • Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)

  • HSA and FSA options

  • Financial wellness resources and employee discount programs


Health & Well-being

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Mental health support for employees and dependents through Lyra Health

  • Family planning and women’s health benefits through Carrot

  • Gym membership reimbursement and virtual wellness programs (including yoga)


Time Off

  • 3 weeks PTO to start, with unlimited PTO after year one


Growth & Development

  • Education expense reimbursement

  • Leadership development programs

  • Certified Payments Professional (CPP) certification support

We believe great performance starts with feeling supported - and we’ve built our benefits with that in mind.

Traditional Physical Requirements:

  • Requires prolonged sitting, standing, bending, stooping and stretching.

  • Requires the ability to lift 10 pounds.

  • Requires eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity and a normal range of hearing and vision (with or without correction).

Join our team at Priority Technology Holdings, Inc. and be part of a dynamic and innovative company that is transforming the financial technology landscape. Together, we can shape the future of payments and banking solutions while providing unmatched value to our clients.

description:
£70,000 to 90,000 GBP

Bonus

Hybrid WORKING

Senior Technical Security Consultant - Security Architecture

No challenge is too difficult for the Vitesse Team. From complex specification driven requirements to precision manufactured components, Vitesse Systems has the experience and expertise needed to execute.

Our core values of Integrity, Initiative, Impact, and Integration translate to an environment where every team member is valued and rewarded. The mission-critical solutions we design and manufacture at Vitesse make our country and our world safer.

The Role

The primary responsibilities of the Test Engineer are to interface with RF and Mechanical Engineers to develop various test documentation, assist technicians with setup and execution of tests, as well as providing support, training, and troubleshooting to the technicians.


Key Responsibilities

  • Plan, perform, and ensure the quality of RF Bench, Near field and Far field Radiation Patterns, Passive Intermodulation, High RF Power, Thermal Vacuum, and other tests on systems and components in accordance with test procedures.
  • Develop test requirements and verification methods through close collaboration with the RF, Mechanical, and Systems Engineering teams.
  • Identify testing methods and test fixturing for risk mitigation, prototype development and requirement verification testing.
  • Collaborate interdepartmentally to review and approve Test Plans, Test Procedures, and Test Reports.

  • Generate and review test plans, test procedures, and review test reports.
  • Assist with technical proposals.
  • Develop and configure methods to efficiently process data and control RF test equipment
  • Provide project support including, but not limited to: design reviews, presentations, data reviews, and production support.
  • Provide auxiliary support as a Test Technician as required.
  • Provide support, training, and troubleshooting to Test Technicians as required.
  • Provide training & mentorship to lower level test engineers.
  • Create and update I&T-related Work Instructions and Processes.
  • Other duties as assigned


Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Physics, Math, or related discipline
  • 8 years minimum industry experience
  • Strong familiarity with RF test equipment and measurement techniques
  • Strong familiarity with communication systems and RF/microwave components
  • Familiarity with environmental test methods, systems, and equipment
  • Familiar with creating budgets for test uncertainties and RF power/link analysis
  • Programming/scripting skills
  • Good bookkeeping and data management skills
  • Good interpersonal and communication skills
  • Comfort working both independently and within a team environment


Vitesse Systems, LLC performs work controlled by the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR). These statutes require the protection of technical data and products. The regulations require that such data not be disclosed in written, oral, or visual form to any foreign national without prior export authorization from the Department of State. A foreign national is defined by the U.S. Government under EAR 734.2(b)(2)(ii) and 8 USC 110 (a)(20) as one who:

  • Is not a United States citizen
  • Is not lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the U.S.
  • Does not have politically protected status (embassy, refugee, or asylum)

title: Research Scientist 2 - Process (Sustainable Materials)
description:
Research Scientist 2 - Process Chemistry (Sustainable Materials)
Salary: £33,727 - £43,727 per annum (dependent on experience)
Employment Type: Full Time, Permanent
Location: Sedgefield

The Role:


This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced laboratory scientist with a strong chemistry background to join a growing and evolving team.


Unlike highly specialised chemistry roles, this position requires someone who is comfortable applying fundamental chemistry principles across a range of different projects and technical challenges. One week you may be supporting materials development activities, another you could be assisting with process optimisation, laboratory investigations, battery material synthesis, analytical testing or helping establish new technical capabilities within a developing facility.
We're looking for someone who enjoys variety, is comfortable working in situations where the path forward is not always clearly defined, and can confidently contribute practical laboratory expertise wherever it is needed.
The successful candidate will predominantly support sustainable materials programmes, although projects may span a broad range of chemistries and technologies as business needs evolve.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Planning, conducting and reporting laboratory-based experimental work.
  • Supporting the development, optimisation and scale-up of chemical processes and materials.
  • Carrying out bench-scale chemistry activities with a high degree of precision and attention to detail.
  • Supporting projects involving sustainable materials, battery materials, polymers and related technologies.
  • Performing synthesis, characterisation, formulation and analytical testing activities.
  • Analysing and interpreting experimental data to support project decision-making.
  • Maintaining accurate laboratory records, technical reports and supporting documentation.
  • Contributing to the establishment of new laboratory capabilities and technical facilities.
  • Working across multiple projects and adapting to changing technical priorities.
  • Collaborating with multidisciplinary scientists, engineers and external partners.
  • Ensuring compliance with Safety, Health and Environmental (SHE) requirements at all times.


About You:
We're looking for a practical scientist who combines strong chemistry fundamentals with a flexible and proactive mindset.
You will likely have:

  • A degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science or a related scientific discipline.
  • Around 2-5 years of relevant laboratory, industrial or research experience.
  • A strong foundation in chemistry gained through academic or industrial experience.
  • Excellent laboratory technique and a commitment to producing high-quality experimental results.
  • Experience documenting, analysing and reporting technical data.
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing project requirements.
  • A collaborative approach and willingness to support colleagues across different technical areas.


Particularly Relevant Experience:
We welcome applications from candidates with backgrounds in either organic or inorganic chemistry, although experience in the following areas would be particularly beneficial:

  • Inorganic chemistry
  • Materials chemistry
  • Sustainable materials development
  • Energy and battery materials
  • Co-precipitation processes
  • Polymer synthesis or polymerisation
  • Formulation science
  • Characterisation techniques
  • Analytical and bench-scale chemistry
  • Titrations and routine laboratory analysis
  • Process development and scale-up


Security Requirements
The successful candidate may work on projects that require security clearance and therefore must be capable of obtaining appropriate clearances where required.

Why Join CPI?
This role offers the opportunity to become part of a highly collaborative team working at the forefront of sustainable materials innovation. You'll gain exposure to a diverse range of projects, technologies and customers while developing your technical expertise in a dynamic research environment.


This would particularly suit a scientist who enjoys hands-on laboratory work, thrives on variety and wants to apply their chemistry knowledge across a broad spectrum of scientific challenges rather than being confined to a single specialism.

The successful candidate will evaluate current encrypted-email and large-file-transfer requirements, assess Microsoft-native solutions, identify any remaining capability gaps and recommend an appropriate target architecture. You will work closely with technical teams and business stakeholders to balance security, compliance, cost, usability and the customer and partner experience.

  • Assess the current use of Echoworx BeSecure, including secure email, encrypted communications and large-file-transfer use cases.

  • Assess and recommend appropriate use of Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Information Protection, sensitivity labels and encryption.
  • Evaluate Microsoft-native capabilities against existing requirements and identify where they can replace or reduce reliance on specialist solutions.

title: MACHINE LEARNING AND OPERATIONS CONSULTANCY
company: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
description:
THE ORGANIZATION
The Alliance of Bioversity International () and the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) () delivers research-based solutions that harness agricultural biodiversity and sustainably transform food systems to improve people’s lives. Alliance solutions address the global crises of malnutrition, climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation.

With novel partnerships, the Alliance generates evidence and mainstreams innovations to transform food systems and landscapes so that they sustain the planet, drive prosperity, and nourish people in a climate crisis.

The Alliance is part of CGIAR, a global research partnership for a food-secure future.

Background:
The NDIZI (NLP to Develop and Innovate Zero-shot Intelligence) project seeks a dedicated Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) Consultant (“the consultant”) to support the development, deployment, and operationalization of machine learning systems powering SIKIA, a voice-first and multimodal AI platform for conversational data collection and analysis, and related AI-driven research workflows. The consultant will work across speech, NLP, multimodal AI, and Agentic pipelines, helping transition models and data systems from research prototypes into reliable, scalable solutions suitable for real-world field deployment.
We are building these systems to enable crop improvement systems to bridge formal breeding processes happening within controlled experimental trials with real-world environments on-farm. Principal use-cases include identifying farmer preferences, assessing plant disease occurrence and scoring, and environmental response - particularly related to climate adaptation. Outputs from this consultancy will be used to address these use-cases.

About the position:
The consultant will support end-to-end MLOps workflows spanning data ingestion, validation, dataset versioning, model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement across both cloud and edge environments. The role will involve close collaboration with research machine learning, software engineering, product, and field teams to ensure systems are robust, maintainable, and aligned with project needs.
The consultant will also support integration of ML systems within the SIKIA platform, including deployment workflows connecting mobile applications, cloud infrastructure, speech and multimodal pipelines, disease detection and severity scoring workflows, backend services, and FAIRGrounds-integrated systems. In addition, the role will contribute to strengthening best practices around experiment tracking, model governance, CI/CD workflows, deployment automation, and ML system monitoring across NDIZI infrastructure.
This is a 11-month full-time consultancy position (with potential for extension) based at the Alliance office in Arusha, Tanzania.

Key Activities and Specific Terms of Reference
Speech and NLP Systems Refinement
● Support deployment and optimization of multilingual ASR pipelines for cloud and mobile environments.
● Develop workflows for speech data ingestion, transcription, evaluation, and continuous model improvement.
● Implement automated retraining and fine-tuning pipelines using newly collected field data.
● Support deployment of LLM-based workflows for conversational analysis and trait extraction.
● Monitor model performance, latency, reliability, and drift under field conditions.
● Optimize inference workflows for low-connectivity and resource-constrained environments.
Multimodal Pipeline Development and Deployment
● Support development of multimodal pipelines linking speech, transcripts, metadata, and field images collected through SIKIA.
● Implement workflows for multimodal data validation, synchronization, storage, annotation, and dataset versioning.
● Support training, deployment, and evaluation of multimodal and visual-language AI models.
● Develop scalable workflows for managing multimodal datasets and model outputs across cloud infrastructure.
● Support benchmarking, reproducibility, and optimization of multimodal AI pipelines for field deployment.

Disease Detection and Severity Scoring
● Support development and deployment of AI workflows for disease detection and severity scoring using field images and multimodal data.
● Implement data and evaluation pipelines for disease annotation, validation, benchmarking, and continuous model improvement.
● Support integration of disease scoring workflows within the SIKIA and ONA platforms for field-based data collection and analysis.
MLOps Infrastructure and SIKIA Integration
● Develop CI/CD pipelines for model training, evaluation, and deployment.
● Manage experiment tracking, model registries, and dataset versioning workflows.
● Implement monitoring and logging across ML services.
● Collaborate with the software development team to integrate RAG pipelines into an Agentic deployment structure.
● Support deployment of ML services on GCP, FAIRGrounds, and related infrastructure.
● Support integration of ML services within the SIKIA platform across mobile, backend, API, and cloud systems.
● Ensure compliance with data governance, security, and responsible AI requirements.

Deliverables and Payment Schedule:
Deliverable 1:Inception Report and Technical Work plan (Month 1, ~Week 4)
Develop an inception report outlining the technical approach, deployment priorities, infrastructure requirements, integration roadmap, and detailed 11-month work plan for MLOps, speech, multimodal, and disease-scoring workflows across the SIKIA platform.
Honoraria for Deliverable 1: 12,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings/ 589,762 Kenyan Shillings.

Deliverable 2: Model Development, Evaluation, and Infrastructure Setup (Month 5, ~Week 20)
Establish core MLOps infrastructure and workflows, including CI/CD pipelines, experiment tracking, dataset versioning, model registries, and monitoring systems. Support development, evaluation, and optimization of speech, multimodal, and disease-scoring models across cloud and edge environments.
Honoraria for Deliverable 2: 18,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings/ 884,642Kenyan Shillings.

Deliverable 3: SIKIA AI Pipeline Integration and Deployment (Month 8, ~Week 32)
Deliver integrated deployment workflows connecting ML services with SIKIA mobile applications, APIs, backend systems, and FAIRGrounds-integrated infrastructure. Provide operational pipelines for speech processing, conversational analysis, multimodal workflows, and disease-scoring services, including deployment documentation and integration support.
Honoraria for Deliverable 3: 22,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings/ 1,081,230 Kenyan Shillings.

Deliverable 4: Monitoring, Evaluation, and Optimization Framework (Month 10, ~Week 40)
Implement monitoring, logging, benchmarking, and evaluation workflows for deployed ML systems, including ASR performance tracking, multimodal pipeline evaluation, disease-scoring validation, and model drift monitoring. Provide recommendations for optimization, scalability, and field deployment improvements.
Honoraria for Deliverable 4: 16,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings/ 786,349 Kenyan Shillings.

Deliverable 5: Final Technical Report and Handover Package (Month 11, end of assignment)
Submit a final technical report summarizing completed workflows, deployed infrastructure, system performance, key learnings, and recommendations for future scaling and maintenance. Deliver finalized documentation, deployment guides, pipeline configurations, and knowledge-transfer materials for internal teams.
Honoraria for Deliverable 5: 22,000,000 Tanzanian Shillings/ 1,081,230 Kenyan Shillings.

Requirements

Education:
Master’s degree in computer science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, or a related field.
Experience:
At least 3 years of experience in Machine Learning engineering, MLOps, or deployment of AI systems.

Technical Competencies:
• Experience building and managing ML workflows, including model training, deployment, monitoring, and versioning.
• Strong programming skills in Python and familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
• Experience working with cloud platforms such as GCP, AWS, or Azure.
• Strong experience with NLP, speech technologies, conversational AI, or LLM-based applications.
• Experience with multimodal AI, computer vision, or image-based AI workflows is desirable.
• Ability to work collaboratively across technical, product, and field teams.
• Strong communication, documentation, and problem-solving skills.
• Background or experience in agriculture, digital agriculture, or international research environments will be an added advantage.

Benefits

Terms of employment

title: waste management officer camps (m/f) - 1 job
description:
Our Client is a multinational company operating in the energy sector.

FUNCTION

Answering to the Facilities Manager and the Waste Management Coordinator, the main activities of the Waste Management Officer Camps include: to monitor and control the day-to-day activities of the waste Contractor within the assigned zone on behalf of the Company; to verify that Contractor activities are executed in accordance with the contract and with approved procedures and method statements, covering collection frequency and routing, crew manning, competence, personal protective equipment, vehicle and equipment condition, load securing and housekeeping; identify any deviation from a contractual clause or approved procedure, stop unsafe or non-compliant activity, report it to the Waste Management Coordinator and support follow-up and closure of corrective actions; provide the factual field evidence, including photographic records, required to support non-conformances and contractual remedies; monitor waste segregation, collection, labeling and storage activities at waste generation points and at the Waste Management Facilities within the zone; verify correct waste classification and compliance with approved waste management procedures for organic, mixed, metal, construction and hazardous streams; verify the number, type, condition, color coding, labeling and signage of bins, skips and containers at each generation point, and require the Contractor to replace or repair damaged or missing containers; identify and correct cross-contamination at the point of generation, record repeat offenders and escalate persistent non-compliance; perform routine inspections of waste storage areas, skips, containers and hazardous waste zones; verify that collection is performed on the agreed schedule and route, with the correct vehicles and equipment, before containers reach overflow; witness loading, weighing and transfer, and confirm that quantities and stream types recorded on manifests and transfer notes match what was collected; track internal waste movements and support verification of waste manifests, registers and certificates; inspect satellite accumulation points in the zone for compliant storage, covering segregation and compatibility, secondary containment and bunding, labeling, closed containers, weather protection and maximum storage duration; verify that spill kits are present, complete and serviceable, and respond to and report spills, leaks and poor practices; conduct routine environmental inspections related to waste within the zone and ensure field data, inspection checklists and photographic records are accurately completed and archived; collect and submit accurate field data for waste quantities, segregation compliance and treatment activities; submit a daily zone report to the Waste Management Coordinator covering collections completed and missed, quantities by stream, segregation compliance, contamination events, container and equipment defects and outstanding actions; contribute to weekly and monthly environmental reporting by providing verified field inputs, and support internal audits, inspections and site visits; deliver toolbox talks and awareness briefings to waste generators in the zone, including camp staff, kitchens, workshops, warehouses and construction crews, on segregation requirements and common errors; raise awareness among Contractors and site personnel on waste segregation and environmental good practices; apply and promote the Site HSE Golden Rules and environmental best practices in daily activities, and work in accordance with permit to work, traffic management, manual handling and personal protective equipment requirements; immediately report incidents, near misses and environmental deviations.

Requirements

  • Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Management, Environmental Science, or related discipline;
  • Field experience in waste management and/or water-wastewater operations (preferably on industrial or construction sites);
  • Basic understanding of environmental permits, waste classification, and wastewater treatment principles;
  • Good communication skills (English is required, while Portuguese is an asset);
  • Ability to conduct field inspections and prepare clear, factual reports;
  • Familiarity with HSE requirements and safe working practices;
  • Ability to work in a remote, multicultural, and high-activity site environment.

Benefits

The possibility of working in a Company that offers salary conditions compatible with the level of experience and level of responsibility of the role, as well as opportunities for personal development.

APPLICATION DEADLINE: October the 15th of 2026.

title: Materials & Inventory Coordinator

The Materials & Inventory Coordinator supports material planning, inventory control, receiving, tracking, and coordination of materials to ensure the timely availability of components and supplies needed for production and operations.

About Vitesse Systems

Vitesse Systems is a leading provider of highly engineered antenna, thermal management and mission critical solutions used in radar, electronic warfare and C5ISR applications. title: Senior Research Scientist 1 - Process Chemistry (Polymers)
description:
Senior Research Scientist 1 - Process Chemistry (Polymers)
Salary: £34,500 - £46,500 per annum (dependent on experience)
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Location: Sedgefield

The Role:


This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced synthetic chemist to join CPI's Process Chemistry team as a technical specialist in polymer and process development.
We're looking for individuals with strong practical chemistry experience who are confident designing, developing and scaling chemical processes beyond the traditional bench environment. The successful candidates will contribute to a broad range of customer and collaborative R&D programmes, with a particular focus on polymer synthesis, process development and scale-up.


A key aspect of the role will involve supporting projects relating to acrylic polymerisation, vinyl monomer chemistry and sustainable materials development. You'll work closely with multidisciplinary teams to develop robust, scalable and safe chemical processes while helping customers overcome complex technical challenges.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Leading technical delivery across small and medium-sized process chemistry projects.
  • Designing, planning and executing experimental programmes focused on polymer and process development.
  • Developing and optimising polymerisation reactions and synthetic routes.
  • Supporting scale-up activities from laboratory development through to pilot-scale operations.
  • Working safely with reactive, corrosive, oxidising and exothermic chemistries.
  • Conducting hazard reviews, risk assessments and process safety activities.
  • Analysing experimental data and translating observations into meaningful process improvements.
  • Producing high-quality technical reports and project documentation.
  • Acting as a technical specialist within project teams and supporting junior scientists.
  • Collaborating with customers, business development teams and external partners on new opportunities.
  • Contributing to the growth of CPI's polymer chemistry and sustainable materials capabilities.


About You:


We are looking for a practical, hands-on chemist who combines strong laboratory skills with experience of process development and scale-up.


You will likely have:

  • A degree, MSc or PhD in Chemistry, Polymer Science, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science or a related discipline.
  • Industrial experience within process chemistry, polymer chemistry or chemical development.
  • A strong background in synthetic chemistry.
  • Experience designing and executing laboratory-based experimental programmes.
  • The ability to solve complex technical problems and interpret experimental results.
  • Excellent communication and technical reporting skills.
  • Experience working collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams.
  • A proactive approach and the confidence to work independently on technical challenges.


Particularly Relevant Experience
We would be especially interested in candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Polymer synthesis
  • Acrylic polymerisation
  • Vinyl or phenyl monomer chemistry
  • Small molecule synthesis
  • Radical polymerisation
  • Process development and optimisation
  • Pilot-scale or industrial-scale chemistry
  • Scale-up within reactor-based environments
  • Hazardous chemical processes
  • Process safety, hazard reviews and troubleshooting
  • Sustainable materials development
  • Advanced materials manufacturing


What We're Looking For:


This role would suit someone who:

  • Has developed a strong chemistry foundation through industry or applied research.
  • Enjoys taking ownership of technical challenges.
  • Is comfortable moving from laboratory work into larger-scale process development.
  • Understands how to safely operate and develop potentially hazardous chemistry.
  • Can balance scientific rigour with practical delivery.
  • Wants to build expertise in polymer process development and scale-up within a highly collaborative environment.


Why Join CPI?


This is an opportunity to join a growing process chemistry team working on commercially relevant projects that help bring innovative and sustainable technologies to market.
You'll work with experienced scientists and engineers across a diverse portfolio of projects, gaining exposure to advanced materials, polymer technologies, process scale-up and future manufacturing. If you're an experienced polymer or synthetic chemist looking to take the next step in your career while working on technically challenging and impactful projects, we'd love to hear from you.

If you have been referred by a CPI employee, please apply through us and email

title: Guidance Counselor
description:
Siena is seeking a K-8 School Counselor for the 26/27 school year and beyond. Our schools are private Catholic schools in Racine, WI which boasts small class sizes and a nurturing family feel. Our schools are part of the Siena Catholic Schools of Racine. Siena Catholic Schools of Racine includes six elementary/middle schools and one high school that serve more than 1,600 students. Sharing your skills will guide the organization toward its goal of ensuring excellence in academics, nurturing faith formation, and developing healthy students.


As a Counselor, here is why you should choose Siena Catholic Schools of Racine:
Small class sizes: our average class size is 20 students with a 10:1 student-teacher ratio.
Faith-based approach to education: we believe that when rooted in faith and tradition, students are able to grow in mind, body, and faith.
Diverse urban student population: we value the strengths of the communities we are a part of.
Focus on graduation and life: we nurture lifelong learners who are prepared to be successful leaders in college, career, community, and the Church.

Scope and Summary:
The guidance counselor is a key person in making the school’s philosophy, mission, and guiding principles come alive for the school community. The counselor challenges all students to develop their God-given talents and achieve their highest potential and works collaboratively with staff to develop a professional learning community. We are currently seeking an outstanding Guidance Counselor to join our dynamic team.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

- Communicate with students and parents in an appropriate and timely manner to inform them of the student’s social and/or academic progress.
- Supports the mission of the school and contributes through personal example to the faith life and values of the school.
- Supervises students as assigned and whenever in the presence of students within the building, on campus or at school events off campus; takes action to deal with any observed, inappropriate student behavior.
- Incorporates faith development opportunities within the instructional program.
- Maintains a presence that provides the necessary and reasonable precautions to ensure student safety and to protect equipment, materials, and facilities.
- Displays respect and sensitivity to the beliefs, ideas, and needs of others.
- Supports and contributes to the continuing development of the school’s programs such as the School Improvement Plan, Staff Development, Campus Ministry, and Extracurriculars.
- Attends all faculty/staff meetings unless excused in advance by the administration.
- Performs all duties and fulfills the responsibilities as specified by the contract and job description, Employee Manual, and Staff and Family Handbooks.
- Performs other duties as assigned by the Administration.

Qualifications:

- Have a Master’s Degree in Guidance Counseling
- Certified by the Wisconsin DPI with License 7054 School Counselor or certifiable according to NCA standards for the position assigned. (If not certified, must have an educational plan, approved by the administration, outlining the steps toward certification with a target completion date. The plan must be on file with the administration.)
- Facility with computer technology including MS Office products and database programs.
- Experience in Catholic education preferred.
- Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with school administrators, faculty, staff, parents, and students in a way which is warm, welcoming, and knowledgeable.
- Highly organized, accountable, confidential, and able to navigate within a diverse environment.
- Ability to work with frequent interruptions and independently with minimal direct supervision.

Physical Requirements: (The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.)
- Communicate verbally; audible speech and good hearing and eyesight
- Read/interpret digital and paper documents
- Physical dexterity to operate computer and equipment

Work Relationships & Scope:
Reports to Principal. Frequent contact with school faculty and staff, students and families. Occasional interaction with other Siena colleagues. Expected to exhibit sound judgment in making decisions, remembering that Siena's interests may be directly affected by their actions and decisions. Secures the approval of the Principal in making decisions when answers are not clear and further guidance or input is needed.

Teachers within our system may also qualify for loan forgiveness

title: Director of Operations
description:
Department: Residential Services

Reports To: Senior Director or Vice President of Residential Services
Location: Greater Bridgewater Area

Hours: 40 per week
FLSA Status: Exempt


Who We Are:
BAMSI has been “bringing people and services together” since 1975. We are a mission-driven nonprofit organization providing critical residential and community-based services to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities across Massachusetts. Our Residential Services team is committed to person-centered care, safety, and quality of life for every individual we serve.


Why This Role Matters:


The Director of Residential Operations provides strategic and operational leadership across a portfolio of residential programs serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. This role is responsible for ensuring high-quality service delivery, regulatory compliance, workforce stability, financial oversight, and operational performance across assigned programs. The Director leads and develops Residential Program Managers and frontline leadership teams while driving consistency, accountability, and person-centered practices throughout residential operations.

What You'll Do:


Leadership & Operations

  • Provide direct supervision, coaching, and leadership to Residential Managers and program leadership teams across assigned residential programs.
  • Ensure programs operate in compliance with DDS, CARF, Medicaid, licensing, and BAMSI policies, procedures, and operational standards.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, engagement, inclusion, and person-centered care across all assigned programs.
  • Provide operational oversight related to staffing, scheduling, coverage planning, workforce stabilization, and vacancy management.
  • Support Residential Managers in addressing staffing concerns, employee relations matters, performance improvement, and team development in collaboration with Human Resources.
  • Provide interim operational leadership and crisis support during management vacancies, staffing shortages, or emergency situations.
  • Participate in on-call rotation and provide leadership response for program emergencies, incidents, staffing escalations, and operational concerns.


Quality & Compliance

  • Ensure quality assurance systems are maintained across programs, including documentation, treatment plans, ISP compliance, medication administration oversight, safety protocols, and incident management.
  • Monitor program performance through audits, operational reviews, corrective action planning, and regulatory readiness activities.
  • Ensure programs maintain compliance with all required trainings, certifications, and credentialing requirements, including CPR/First Aid, MAP, safety trainings, and behavior management certifications.
  • Partner with Quality Assurance, Clinical, Nursing, and Human Rights teams to ensure services support the behavioral, medical, and clinical needs of individuals served.


Financial & Administrative Oversight

  • Oversee program budgets, financial performance, overtime utilization, purchasing, and operational expenses across assigned programs.
  • Review financial and operational reports regularly to identify trends, risks, staffing concerns, and opportunities for improved efficiency.
  • Ensure administrative systems and operational processes are maintained in areas including payroll, electronic health records, scheduling systems, documentation compliance, and transportation coordination.
  • Support operational planning related to admissions, discharges, transfers, program openings, and service transitions.


Workforce Development & Talent Management

  • Lead hiring, onboarding, succession planning, and leadership development efforts for Residential Managers and program leadership staff.
  • Foster employee engagement through coaching, recognition, mentorship, and professional development initiatives.
  • Conduct regular supervision meetings and performance evaluations while ensuring leadership teams meet established performance expectations.
  • Support recruitment and retention initiatives designed to strengthen workforce stability and reduce turnover across residential operations.


Community & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Maintain positive relationships with individuals served, families, guardians, funding sources, external providers, and community stakeholders.
  • Support programs in building inclusive community engagement opportunities and positive neighborhood relationships.
  • Participate in agency committees, leadership meetings, and strategic operational initiatives as assigned.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.


What We Offer:

  • Competitive Compensation: A salary commensurate with your experience and expertise.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Full benefits package including generous PTO, health/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, and a 403(b) with company match.
  • Leadership Impact: The opportunity to shape residential operations and drive meaningful change across multiple programs.
  • Mission-Driven Culture: The satisfaction of knowing your leadership directly enhances the quality of life for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.


What You Bring (Requirements):

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Human Services, Healthcare Administration, Social Work, Psychology, Business Administration, or related field required. Master's degree preferred. In lieu of a bachelor’s degree, substantial senior supervisory experience in human services may be considered.
  • Experience: Minimum of 5–7 years of experience working within residential or human services operations supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
  • Leadership Experience: Minimum of 3–5 years of progressive leadership experience supervising managers, multi-site operations, or residential programs.
  • Financial Acumen: Experience managing program budgets, staffing operations, compliance standards, and workforce performance required.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: Strong understanding of DDS regulations, CARF standards, person-centered supports, behavior management principles, and residential operations required.
  • Requirements: Valid driver's license with acceptable driving history required.

Required Skills & Competencies:

  • Strong operational leadership and organizational management skills
  • Ability to lead through change and manage competing priorities in fast-paced environments
  • Strong conflict resolution, coaching, and employee relations skills
  • Knowledge of residential licensing, regulatory compliance, and quality assurance practices
  • Financial management and budget oversight experience
  • Strong communication, documentation, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to analyze operational trends and implement corrective actions
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, scheduling systems, electronic health records, and workforce management systems
  • Ability to build collaborative partnerships across departments and leadership teams
  • Ability to respond effectively during emergencies and operational crises

Physical Requirements:


The physical demands of this role may include supporting residential programs in environments requiring movement assistance, behavioral intervention support, emergency response, and active participation in program operations. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions. The employee may be required to:

  • Climb stairs
  • Assist individuals with mobility and daily living activities
  • Lift or support individuals as needed during emergency situations
  • Drive agency vehicles, including passenger vans and wheelchair-accessible vehicles
