  • Build and enhance Splunk dashboards to support operational monitoring and management reporting.
  • Review and tune detection logic to reduce false positives and convert high-volume monitoring data into targeted, actionable alerts.
  • Develop and refine DLP correlation searches and detection use cases to improve monitoring effectiveness.
  • Create clear documentation covering searches, dashboards, alert logic, correlation use cases and operational processes.
  • Produce and maintain runbooks to support consistent operations and knowledge retention within the internal team.
  • Work independently to identify monitoring improvements and deliver practical enhancements across the DLP capability.
  • Support junior analysts through technical guidance, knowledge sharing and knowledge transfer.
  • Establish a sustainable approach to DLP reporting, alerting and ongoing monitoring improvements.
Essential Skills and Experience
  • Strong hands-on Splunk engineering experience.
  • Advanced SPL skills, including complex searches and multi-index correlation.
  • Experience building Splunk dashboards, drilldowns and alerts.
  • Practical experience working with DLP-related indexes and data sources.
  • Ability to correlate multiple DLP data sources into meaningful views of user activity, incidents and control outcomes.
  • Experience tuning detection logic and reducing false-positive alerts.
  • Ability to translate high-volume monitoring data into targeted, actionable security alerts.
  • Experience developing operational dashboards and management reporting.
  • Strong documentation skills, including search documentation, operational procedures and runbooks.
  • Ability to work independently, manage technical improvements and transfer knowledge to junior analysts.
Expected Deliverables
  • Improved DLP monitoring dashboards and management reports.
  • Refined detection alerts and DLP correlation use cases.
  • Better correlation of user activity, incidents and control outcomes across multiple data sources.
  • Reduced false positives and more actionable alerts.
  • Documented Splunk searches, processes and operational runbooks.
  • A sustainable reporting and monitoring capability that the internal team can maintain.

  • London, UK.
  • Hybrid working, with three days per week onsite at the client’s office.

description:
Electrical Multiskilled Engineer / Wirral, Merseyside / £45,000 per annum
Working Hours: Monday–Thursday, 8:00am–5:00pm; Friday, 8:00am–12:30pm

Take Your Engineering Career to the Next Level!

Are you an experienced Electrical Multiskilled Engineer looking for a challenging, hands-on role where your technical expertise can make a real difference?

Our client is seeking a skilled engineer to join their manufacturing operation on the Wirral, taking responsibility for electrical maintenance, fault finding, repairs and equipment improvements across the site.

This is an excellent opportunity for a technically minded engineer who enjoys solving problems, improving equipment reliability and working in a fast-paced industrial environment. With a competitive £45,000 salary and an early finish every Friday, this role also offers an attractive working pattern.

The Electrical Multiskilled Engineer Role

As an Electrical Multiskilled Engineer, you'll play a key role in keeping production equipment and site services running safely, efficiently and reliably.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Carrying out planned preventative maintenance (PPM), electrical repairs and installations across the site.
  • Diagnosing and resolving electrical faults on production machinery, control systems and associated equipment.
  • Working with PLC-controlled equipment, HMIs, variable-speed drives, motors, sensors and safety circuits.
  • Responding to breakdowns and identifying opportunities to improve equipment reliability and reduce downtime.
  • Delivering small engineering projects, including equipment installations, control modifications and machinery improvements.
  • Reading electrical drawings and maintaining accurate maintenance records and technical documentation.
  • Supporting mechanical maintenance and repairs within your competence.
  • Following safe isolation, lockout, permit-to-work and change-control procedures.
  • Working collaboratively with production teams, contractors and fellow engineers to maintain high standards of safety and workmanship.

What We're Looking For

You'll be an experienced electrical engineer with a strong manufacturing background, confident working independently to diagnose faults and deliver effective engineering solutions.

Essential requirements:

  • Minimum NVQ Level 3 in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Installation or a relevant electrical discipline.
  • 18th Edition Wiring Regulations qualification.
  • Recognised electrical apprenticeship or equivalent practical training.
  • At least five years' relevant electrical engineering experience within a manufacturing environment.
  • Strong electrical fault-finding skills, including experience with industrial machinery and control systems.
  • Experience of PPM, breakdown response and electrical installations.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics.
  • Practical mechanical maintenance skills.
  • A thorough understanding of safe isolation and electrical working practices.

Desirable Experience

  • CompEx Ex01–Ex04 qualification.
  • Experience within aerosol, chemical or other hazardous-area manufacturing environments.
  • Knowledge of ATEX equipment and DSEAR requirements.
  • Experience delivering engineering projects and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Familiarity with computerised maintenance management systems (CMMS).

What's on Offer?

  • £45,000 annual salary.
  • Salary sacrifice on pension
  • Free parking
  • Free weekly fruit
  • Simply health cash plan
  • Team building day annually
  • Day-shift working pattern.
  • Early finish every Friday at 12:30pm.
  • A varied, hands-on engineering role with opportunities to contribute to equipment improvements and operational efficiency.
  • The opportunity to apply your technical skills within an established manufacturing environment.

Interested?

If you're a qualified Electrical Multiskilled Engineer who enjoys fault finding, solving technical challenges and keeping production running at its best, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to take the next step in your engineering career on the Wirral.

title: Senior Rust Engineer
description:
Rust Software Engineer | Up to £130,000 | Remote

About the Role

My client, a pioneering UK technology firm redefining global communication networks. They are building solutions that operate where standard systems fail — powering resilient, far-reaching connectivity across critical environments.

They are seeking a Rust Engineer to join their core R&D team and lead development of the next generation of their tech stack and platform. You will write high-performance, production-grade Rust that directly shapes how networks run worldwide.

This isn’t just coding — you’ll build systems that solve genuinely complex problems for customers and partners across the globe.

What You’ll Be Building

  • Develop and maintain high-performance DTN products, platforms, and APIs — predominantly in Rust — using gRPC and Protocol Buffers
  • Architect and scale distributed, cloud-native systems running on Kubernetes
  • Own code from design through to production: implement, debug, test, and optimise
  • Modernise and evolve existing capabilities with cutting-edge approaches
  • Collaborate across full-stack teams to pair robust backend logic with seamless user experiences
  • Translate technical and commercial needs into elegant, maintainable Rust solutions
  • Create documentation, tutorials, and sample code to empower developers and customers using The Relay Network
  • Support customer onboarding — guiding integration and ensuring systems perform at scale

What You Bring — Essentials

  • Strong professional experience writing production Rust — you understand idiomatic design, concurrency, and performance characteristics
  • Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related technical discipline
  • Proven ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to engineers, customers, and stakeholders alike
  • Curiosity that goes deeper than code: you want to understand the business and the ecosystem your systems serve
  • Experience working directly with end-users — diagnosing issues, proposing solutions, and building trust
  • A genuine passion for championing great technology

Highly Desirable

title: Product Management Senior Expert
description:
As a Senior Product Manager for one of our Strategic Use Cases, you will own that use case end-to-end — from the customer problem and the data it depends on, through prototype, roadmap and launch, to the outcome in the market. You will work alongside senior engineers and product experts to define the ambition, understand requirements and launch innovative new products.

This is a builder role, not a coordination role. We're looking for a high-agency generalist who prototypes before they debate, uses AI to move at a different speed, engages customers directly, and takes full ownership of outcomes — not output.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the vision: Set and drive the aligned, end-to-end vision for your use case (regulatory due diligence, human rights due diligence, decarbonization or resilience)— what the customer experience should be, where the gaps are, and the sequence from parity to leadership.
  • Understand the market: Understand the technical requirements of your use case, and how other competitors and customers are currently solving it. Take inspiration from everywhere, including partner discussions, conferences, webinars and other resources.
  • Engage customers directly: Spend real time with buyers, program owners and co-development accounts. Validate problems and solutions first-hand; and build interest from customers and prospects.
  • Prototype with AI: Use AI prototyping tools to build working demos, spin up lightweight services and test your own assumptions before committing engineering. Show the team what's possible by doing it, not describing it.
  • Drive the build forward: Work alongside engineering to unblock and drive the build forward, working across multiple areas of the product and platform, collaborating with other tribes and squads whilst executing independently or in partnership.
  • Partner on go-to-market: Work hand-in-hand with the Strategic Use Case Leads and commercial teams to land what you build.
  • Own the outcome: Define the measures of success, hold yourself and the circle to them, and lead clean persist / pivot / stop decisions.

Who you are

  • A generalist builder at heart — you move fluidly between strategy, data, prototype and GTM, and you'd rather build a rough thing that teaches you something than debate a perfect thing that doesn't.
  • An AI-native operator — AI is woven through how you work: discovery, analysis, prototyping, instrumentation and communication.
  • Customer-obsessed — you get your conviction from talking to real customers, not from the building.
  • Biased to speed — you move decisively with incomplete information, tell reversible decisions from irreversible ones, and update fast when you're wrong. Strong opinions, loosely held.
  • Comfortable without full control — part of your use case's scope and experience will always be owned by other squads. You see managing that, as the craft.
  • Mission-driven — you want your work to help guide all companies toward a sustainable world, and to help EcoVadis lead the market in getting there.

AI fluency we hire for

We expect you to operate at the AI-Fluent to AI-Native end of the spectrum: you don't just use AI for one-off tasks, you reconstruct core PM workflows around it — agents configured with your product context, personas and prior research; machine-testable acceptance criteria; reusable workflows you share with the squad. At the top of this ladder, the PM shifts from feature author to outcome orchestrator — concentrating on strategic trade-offs and novel bets while agents carry more of the discovery and synthesis.

  • Typically 10+ years experience, including a track record owning a meaningful product area end-to-end in B2B enterprise SaaS, with real business and customer outcomes to point to.
  • Enough technical fluency to build — you can prototype with AI tooling, LLM APIs and a scripting language (Python / JavaScript or equivalent) without waiting for engineering to validate every idea.
  • An AI-native way of working that's already part of how you operate, not an aspiration.
  • Comfort operating in a regulated, data-rich, sustainability or risk domain — or the curiosity and speed to get there fast.
  • Sharp problem framing and communication — you walk into the room with a recommendation, not an open question, and you make engineering and design faster by reducing ambiguity.
  • Be fluent in English (as our primary working language).

In return for your expertise, we offer:

  • Support with all the necessary office and IT equipment
  • Flexible working hours
  • Wellness allowance for mental and physical wellbeing
  • Access to professional mental health support
  • Referral bonus policy
  • Learning and development
  • Sustainability events and community involvement
  • Peer recognition program
  • Employee-led resource groups
  • Hybrid work organization (2 office days per week)
  • Remote work from abroad policy
  • Meals and Transportation Vouchers (Coverflex card)
  • Dental Benefits
  • Life & Accident Insurance + Private Health Insurance
  • Paid employee volunteer day
  • Paid moving day (1/year)
  • Time off: 1 Community Service Day + 1 Personal Day
  • Summer Hours in July and August (36 hours per week)
  • Hybrid Monthly Allowance for electricity and Internet

Our hiring team looks forward to reviewing your resume, in English, with a guaranteed response to every application. A new job with purpose awaits you!

Don’t meet all criteria? Please apply anyway. We welcome diverse candidates and want to assess your skills and potential contribution to EcoVadis, regardless of your background.

Can the hiring process be adjusted to suit my needs? Yes. We want all candidates, including people with disabilities, people with long-term health conditions, and neurodiverse applicants, to feel confident demonstrating their potential. If you require adjustments, such as interview questions in advance, please inform the hiring team.

Our team’s strength comes from everyone’s uniqueness and is founded upon mutual respect. EcoVadis commits to equity, inclusion and reducing bias in our hiring processes. EcoVadis does not accept any form of discrimination based on characteristics such as color, national or ethnic origin, ancestry, citizenship, religion, beliefs, age, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, parental status, or any other protected characteristic that makes you unique. To reduce bias in hiring, applicants are encouraged to remove personal details such as photos, marital/parental status, religion, gender, postal code, university name/graduation date, past leave details, and nationality (instead, confirm eligibility to work in the job location).

Our recruitment processes do not include AI systems that make autonomous decisions impacting individuals’ rights without human oversight. Inputs and outputs of the system have been validated by humans and answers are based on algorithms that analyze previous data with which the system has been trained. We use SmartRecruiters as our applicant tracking system and to schedule interviews. Gemini is used to summarize notes from interviews and to refine job descriptions and social media messaging. AssessFirst is used to support talent assessment decisions.

title: Receiving Lead - 2nd Shift ( Paint )
description:
Why Join Steele Solutions?

At Steele Solutions, we believe our people are the foundation of our success. We are committed to providing a safe workplace, opportunities for growth and advancement, and a culture built on teamwork, innovation, and continuous improvement.

When you join Steele Solutions, you're joining a company that values your contributions, invests in your development, and provides opportunities to build a long-term career. We encourage employees to learn new skills, share ideas, and grow professionally while helping deliver industry-leading solutions for our customers.


What You Can Expect:

  • A safe, quality-focused work environment
  • Opportunities for training, skill development, and career advancement
  • A team-oriented culture built on respect and collaboration
  • Stable employment with a growing organization
  • Leaders who value employee contributions and continuous improvement
  • Meaningful work that directly impacts our customers' success
  • Competitive pay and comprehensive benefits package
  • 401(k) with company match, paid time off, and paid holidays


Position Summary

Under the direction of the Production supervisor, the Receiving Lead is responsible for leading daily receiving operations while ensuring inventory accuracy, efficient material flow, and compliance with company safety and quality standards. This hands-on leadership role supports receiving team members, coordinates incoming materials, and works closely with Production, Purchasing, Quality, and Shipping to ensure materials are received, stored, and delivered in a timely manner.

The Receiving Lead serves as a key resource within the warehouse and manufacturing environment by promoting safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

This list of duties and responsibilities is not all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other responsibilities as management deems necessary.


Leadership & Team Coordination

  • Lead and coordinate daily receiving activities to ensure operational goals are met.
  • Provide training, coaching, and support to receiving team members.
  • Assist with workload distribution and task prioritization.
  • Promote a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
  • Serve as a point of contact for receiving-related issues and problem resolution.

Receiving & Inventory Management

  • Coordinate the receipt of incoming materials, parts, and supplies.
  • Verify shipments against purchase orders, packing slips, and shipping documentation.
  • Inspect incoming materials for damage, defects, and quantity discrepancies.
  • Document and communicate receiving issues to appropriate departments.
  • Ensure all materials are properly scanned and received into the business system.
  • Maintain accurate inventory records and storage locations.
  • Perform cycle counts and support inventory audits.
  • Monitor inventory accuracy and take corrective action when discrepancies are identified.

Material Handling

  • Place incoming materials into designated inventory locations.
  • Pull and deliver materials to production as needed to support manufacturing requirements.
  • Move products and materials throughout the facility using forklifts, cranes, and other material handling equipment.
  • Ensure material handling equipment is inspected and maintained in safe working condition.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Review bills of lading, packing slips, purchase orders, invoices, and other receiving documents.
  • Accurately complete and maintain all required paperwork and system transactions.
  • Maintain compliance with company procedures and quality requirements.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment using 5S principles and best practices.
  • Follow all company safety policies and procedures.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Education and Experience

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • Minimum of 2 years of receiving, warehouse, inventory control, or material handling experience.
  • Previous lead or supervisory experience preferred.
  • Forklift operating experience required; certification preferred.
  • Experience with ERP, warehouse management, or inventory systems preferred.
  • Basic computer skills including data entry, email, and business system navigation.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints, packing slips, and receiving documentation.
  • Ability to accurately use a tape measure and digital measuring tools.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • Commitment to workplace safety and quality standards.
  • Ability to work effectively with employees across multiple departments.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position.

  • Regularly required to stand, walk, bend, reach, and use hands to handle materials.
  • Frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, and crawl.
  • Specific vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this position.

  • Manufacturing and warehouse environment.
  • Exposure to forklifts, cranes, and moving mechanical equipment.
  • Moderate to high noise levels depending on production activity.
  • Required use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Commitment to maintaining a safe, clean, and organized workplace.

The Body Technician is a skilled craftsman with a thorough understanding of how to restore automobiles with light to heavy damage through collision repair. What is Lead Solutions Engineering – Data Center Design & Infrastructure?

The senior data center presales professional responsible for enterprise data center design, infrastructure solution development, technical qualification and customer engagement. The role requires broad understanding of data center architecture, TIA-942 and Uptime Institute Tier III/Rated-3 concepts, active and passive infrastructure, power, cooling/HVAC and telecom infrastructure, with the ability to translate customer requirements into integrated, resilient and scalable designs.   • Lead presales activities for enterprise data center design and infrastructure solutions from requirement discovery through conceptual design, proposal and technical handover.
  • Engage enterprise customers to understand business continuity, availability, capacity, rack density, power, cooling, physical security, connectivity, expansion and operational requirements.
  • Develop data center conceptual and detailed designs covering white space, raised flooring, racks, containment, structured cabling, active/passive network infrastructure, power distribution, UPS, PDU, generators and associated facilities.
  • Apply and interpret relevant data center standards and frameworks, particularly TIA-942 and Uptime Institute Tier III / Rated-3 concepts, while clearly identifying customer-specific design and compliance requirements.
  • Evaluate and design different cooling approaches including conventional precision cooling, in-row cooling, perimeter cooling, containment-based cooling and high-density/liquid-cooling considerations where applicable.
  • Develop power infrastructure concepts including utility feeds, generators, UPS configurations, STS/ATS, PDUs, redundancy, power monitoring and distribution to IT loads.
  • Design telecom and structured cabling infrastructure, including fiber and copper connectivity, pathways, racks, patching and cross-connect considerations.
  • Coordinate active network, compute, storage, security and facilities requirements to ensure an integrated data center architecture.
  • Prepare architecture drawings, layouts, BoQ/BoM, technical specifications, compliance matrices, RFI/RFQ/RFP/tender responses, presentations and technical proposals.
  • Conduct customer workshops and site discussions; perform pre-work, data collection, assumptions, gap analysis and technical risk identification.
  • Engage OEMs, distributors, OEM partners, system integrators, contractors and specialist SMEs for solution validation, design inputs, pricing support and technical clarifications.
  • Support solution estimation, TCO discussions, phased expansion planning and future-ready design recommendations.

Key Deliverables

  • Customer data center requirement and discovery documents.
  • Conceptual and detailed data center architecture/design documentation.
  • Power, cooling, rack, cabling, telecom and facilities design inputs.
  • TIA-942 / Uptime Tier III or Rated-3 aligned compliance and requirement matrices, where applicable.
  • BoQ/BoM, technical specifications and tender/RFP/RFI/RFQ responses.
  • Customer presentations, workshops, site assessment inputs and technical clarifications.
  • Integrated active/passive infrastructure design and cross-domain coordination documents.
  • Reference architectures, design standards, reusable templates and technical handover packages.

Jazz is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate, support, and thrive on diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Experience and Educational requirements

  • 6–8 years of relevant data center design, presales, consulting or solution architecture experience, preferably with enterprise customers.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, Telecom, Networking, Mechanical Engineering, Data Center Engineering or another relevant discipline.

  • Understanding of different cooling technologies and their applicability to conventional and high-density IT environments.
  • Ability to interpret power, cooling, rack-density, connectivity and availability requirements and translate them into an integrated design.
  • Relevant data center certifications are preferred, such as Uptime Institute, TIA-942, CDCP/CDCS/CDCE or equivalent recognized certifications.
  • Experience working with multiple OEMs, distributors, OEM partners, system integrators, facilities contractors and specialist vendors.
  • Strong experience in enterprise customer engagement, technical discovery, workshops, presentations, RFI/RFQ/RFP/tender responses and solution proposals.
  • Ability to coordinate multiple SMEs and domains including network, compute, storage, security, power, cooling, structured cabling and telecom.
  • Strong technical documentation, presentation, communication, stakeholder management and project coordination skills.

Soft skills and technical skills required

  • Customer-centric approach with strong consultative selling and requirement-generation capability.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication, presentation and workshop facilitation skills.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and solution-design mindset with ability to simplify complex technical concepts for business stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently while coordinating multiple internal teams, OEMs, distributors, partners and system integrators.
  • Strong ownership, responsiveness, documentation discipline and ability to manage multiple opportunities and deadlines.

title: Software & AI Engineer
description:
Software & AI Engineer - JD

Company Name: Alethic Insights
Website: Alethic Insights | Executive Intelligence Systems
LinkedIn: Alethic Insights | LinkedIn

If you love owning full-stack products end-to-end, thrive on building production-grade Python services and polished React interfaces, and get genuinely excited about LLMs and agents actually doing things — this role was written for you.
At our end, we are building our flagship platform that blends data, workflow automation, and agentic AI to help enterprises make smarter decisions, faster. We are looking for a hands-on engineer with 3–6 years of relevant experience who can own services end-to-end: design, build, deploy, monitor, and iterate. You’ll ship production code, shape the architecture, and help us push the boundaries of what agentic AI can do inside a real product.

Why This Role Is Different
• Real ownership. You own modules end-to-end — design, ship, monitor, iterate.
• True full-stack ownership. React frontends, Python APIs, cloud infra, AI pipelines, auth, observability — the whole stack, your call.
• AI that’s more than hype. Build and own RAG pipelines, vector search, LLM integrations, and autonomous agents that do actual work inside a real enterprise product.
• Small team, big leverage. Direct collaboration with senior engineers and the founding team. No layers, no politics.
• Career trajectory. A clear path to senior engineering and tech-lead roles as NUDGE scales.

What You’ll Actually Do
• Own features end-to-end across the full stack. Take a feature from design doc to production — React UI, FastAPI service, database schema, AWS deployment, and monitoring — without handing off to another team. You are the team.
• Build and ship React interfaces that enterprise users actually love. Design and implement component hierarchies, manage state across complex workflows, integrate with REST APIs, handle async data gracefully, and make sure the UI stays responsive even when an AI agent is doing heavy work in the background.
• Design and ship Python/FastAPI services that are built to last. Clean router structure, Pydantic-validated contracts, dependency-injected auth, background task queues (Celery/RQ), async I/O where it matters — and the discipline to write tests before you call something done.
• Implement and own end-to-end RAG pipelines. Not just “plug in LangChain and call it done” — you’ll choose the right chunking strategy for the document type, select and fine-tune embedding models, stand up and query vector stores (Pinecone, pgvector, or Weaviate), add reranking, and instrument retrieval quality metrics so you know when the pipeline degrades in production.
• Build agentic AI workflows that actually complete tasks. Design multi-step agent graphs using LangGraph or similar, wire up tool-calling against internal APIs and external services, handle failure modes and retry logic, and evaluate agent performance — not just “did it finish” but “did it finish correctly.”
• Own the data layer from schema to query plan. Model relational data in PostgreSQL with multi-tenancy and row-level security in mind, write queries a DBA would be proud of, reach for Redis or DynamoDB when the access pattern demands it, and know how to spot an N+1 before it becomes a production incident.
• Deploy and operate your own services on AWS. Containerize with Docker, orchestrate on ECS or Lambda, store secrets in Secrets Manager, wire IAM with least privilege, set up RDS with proper connection pooling, and build CloudWatch dashboards and alarms so you know when something is wrong before a user files a ticket.
• Implement auth you’d stake your reputation on. JWT issuance and validation, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC flows, role-based access control, secure session management, and the habit of asking “can this endpoint be called by the wrong tenant?” before every PR merge.
• Ship with a CI/CD pipeline, not a prayer. Set up GitHub Actions (or equivalent) pipelines that lint, test, build, and deploy — so merging to main means it’s in production, not “it’s waiting for someone to SSH into a box.”

Must-Have Skills
• Generative AI & RAG: you’ve built a RAG pipeline in production — not just followed a tutorial. You understand the tradeoffs between chunking strategies (fixed-size, semantic, document-structure-aware), have selected and compared embedding models, have stood up at least one vector store (Pinecone, pgvector, Weaviate, or Qdrant), and you know that retrieval quality requires measurement, not hope. Fluency with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock) and at least one agent framework (LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex) is expected.
• SQL & data modelling: PostgreSQL is your default. You write joins, window functions, CTEs, and subqueries without hesitation, you understand EXPLAIN ANALYZE output, you design schemas with multi-tenancy in mind, and you don’t wait for a DBA to tell you your query is slow.
• Python & FastAPI: async/await, Pydantic v2, dependency injection, background tasks, structured logging, and the instinct to write a test alongside the feature — not a week later. You can explain the difference between asyncio concurrency and true parallelism, and you know when Celery is the right answer and when it’s overkill.
• Auth & security fundamentals: JWT, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, RBAC, and the habit of auditing every endpoint for tenant isolation before merging. You’ve thought about prompt injection, you know what OWASP Top 10 means in a Python/React context, and you don’t store secrets in environment variables committed to git.
• Systems thinking: you can sketch a multi-service architecture, reason about where state should live, identify single points of failure, and make deliberate tradeoffs between consistency and availability. When to use a queue, when to go synchronous, when Redis is the answer and when it’s a crutch — you have opinions and can defend them.
• Agentic AI: you’ve built agents that do more than answer questions — they plan, decide, call tools, and recover from failures. You understand the difference between single-step tool-calling and multi-step agent graphs (LangGraph, CrewAI, or similar), know how to design reliable tool interfaces, handle partial failures and retries gracefully, manage context window constraints across long-running tasks, and evaluate whether an agent actually completed its goal — not just whether it returned a response. Prompt engineering discipline (system prompts, few-shot examples, structured outputs) is assumed.
• Frontend fundamental: you understand how the web actually works — HTML structure and semantics, CSS layout and specificity, JavaScript (ES6+) including the event loop, promises, and
async/await. You know the full HTTP request/response cycle: methods, status codes, headers, cookies, CORS, and how a browser request travels from the user to your FastAPI service and back. You understand REST vs WebSocket vs SSE and can pick the right protocol for the job. You can read browser DevTools network traces, debug a broken API call from the frontend, and reason about where a problem lives without needing someone to hand you a reproduction. React or another framework is expected on top of this — but the fundamentals come first.

Good-to-Have
• React & TypeScript: functional components, custom hooks, Zustand or Redux for state, React Router, typed API calls with axios or react-query, and clean handling of loading/error/empty states. TypeScript by default. You don’t need a senior frontend engineer reviewing your code for correctness — just for taste.
• LLM evaluation and observability: experience with RAGAS, LangSmith, Phoenix/Arize, or similar tools for measuring retrieval quality, hallucination rates, and agent task completion — not just “it looked right in the demo.”
• Data pipeline experience: ingestion, transformation, and enrichment pipelines (Airflow, AWS Glue, or even just well-structured Celery workflows) — particularly for feeding structured and unstructured data into AI systems at scale.
• Infrastructure as code: Terraform, AWS CDK, or Pulumi — the ability to version and review infrastructure changes the same way you review code. Not required, but the team will love you for it.
• Enterprise SaaS patterns: multi-tenancy, row-level security, usage metering, audit logging, SSO/SAML integration, or experience building for compliance-conscious enterprise buyers. You’ve shipped something to a customer who cares about SOC 2 or GDPR.
• NoSQL and search: DynamoDB for high-throughput key-value access patterns, Redis beyond basic caching (pub/sub, streams, sorted sets), or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for full-text and hybrid search — knowing when to reach past PostgreSQL and why.
• Prior startup or product company experience: you know what it means to own a feature end-to-end with limited resources, make pragmatic tradeoffs under time pressure, and ship to real users who notice when things break.

Who You Are
• 3–6 years of relevant, hands-on experience building and shipping full-stack production applications — backend-heavy is fine, but you should be able to own a React feature without hand-holding. Bonus if some of that experience was at an early-stage product company.
• A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field — or a track record strong enough that we don’t need to ask.
• You’ve owned features (not just tickets) from spec to production, and you have the war stories to prove it.
• You read documentation before you ask questions, and you ask great questions when documentation falls short.
• You care about clean code, code reviews, and the difference between a PR that’s done and one that’s merged.
• You’re curious about AI but skeptical of magic — you want to understand what’s actually happening under the hood.
• You communicate well in writing. Slack messages, PRs, design docs, incident notes — clarity is a superpower.

title: Integration & Test Technician II
description:
Vitesse Systems is looking for an Integration & Test Technician II to join the team in Harbor City, California! The Integration & Test Technician supports the assembly, integration, tuning, testing, and verification of RF microwave and waveguide-based components used in ground station antenna systems.

About Vitesse Systems

Vitesse Systems is a leading provider of highly engineered antenna, thermal management and mission critical solutions used in radar, electronic warfare and C5ISR applications. No challenge is too difficult for the Vitesse Team. From complex specification driven requirements to precision manufactured components, Vitesse Systems has the experience and expertise needed to execute.

Our Core Values

Our core values of Integrity, Initiative, Impact, and Integration translate to an environment where every team member is valued and rewarded. The mission-critical solutions we design and manufacture at Vitesse make our country and our world safer.

The Role

The Integration & Test Technician role is primarily hands-on, with approximately 75% focused on mechanical assembly and integration work and 25% focused on RF testing and verification.

Key Responsibilities

Assembly & Integration

  • Perform assembly and disassembly tasks using hand tools in accordance with travelers, drawings, and work instructions
  • Build Mandrel assemblies and verify electrical conductivity
  • Perform hand mechanical solder operations
  • Assist in integration of waveguide and RF components into subassemblies

Electromechanical Systems

  • Wire electromechanical assemblies such as motors, encoders, and waveguide switches
  • Verify proper functionality of wired systems

RF Testing & Verification

  • Perform tune, test, and verification of RF microwave components
  • Execute RF test procedures and test plans in accordance with engineering requirements
  • Support RF testing activities utilizing vector network analyzers (VNA), spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, and other RF test equipment
  • Assist in troubleshooting basic RF test discrepancies under supervision
  • Verify product performance against established specifications and acceptance

Mechanical Validation & Quality

  • Perform sealing operations and leak test verifications
  • Inspect assemblies for workmanship and compliance with specifications
  • Document test results and report discrepancies

Workplace & Compliance

  • Follow all applicable procedures, work instructions, and safety guidelines
  • Responsible for maintaining a clean and organized work area in compliance with 5S, including cleanup after task completion

Success Metrics

  • Throughput (units completed vs. plan)
  • On-Time completion of assigned work orders/travelers
  • First-pass yield (builds passing inspection without rework

Other duties as assigned


Qualifications & Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • 2+ years of mechanical assembly experience within aerospace, satellite communications, defense, or related manufacturing environments preferred
  • Engineering Degree is a plus
  • Ability to read and comprehend mechanical blueprints
  • General knowledge of RF measurement equipment and techniques preferred
  • Familiarity with RF measurements equipment and techniques preferred
  • Experience with hand tools
  • Experience with SolidWorks/CAD is a plus/CAD
  • High attention to detail
  • Interest in mechanical assembly or technical work
  • Familiarity with basic inspection tools (calipers, micrometers, etc)
  • Prior experience in machining, or inspection
  • Awareness of aerospace quality standards (AS9100 or similar)
  • Strong work ethic and willingness to learn
  • Good attention to detail and pride in hands-on work
  • Ability to follow instructions and work in a team environment
  • Good hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity
  • Dependable, punctual, and consistent in completing assigned tasks
  • Positive attitude and openness to feedback and training

Vitesse Systems, LLC performs work controlled by the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR). These statutes require the protection of technical data and products. The regulations require that such data not be disclosed in written, oral, or visual form to any foreign national without prior export authorization from the Department of State. A foreign national is defined by the U.S. Government under EAR 734.2(b)(2)(ii) and 8 USC 110 (a)(20) as one who:

  • Is not a United States citizen
  • Is not lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the U.S.
  • Does not have politically protected status (embassy, refugee, or asylum)

title: Senior Technical Coach - Hire Train Deploy - La Fosse Academy
description:
At La Fosse Academy, we help people from a wide range of backgrounds build successful careers in technology.

Through our Hire, Train, Deploy model, we identify potential, develop practical technical and professional skills, and support associates as they move into roles with our client organisations. Our training prepares people to contribute in the workplace, combining technical knowledge with the confidence, communication and problem-solving skills they need to succeed.

We’re looking for a Senior Technical Coach to join our training team and help develop the next generation of technology professionals.

About the role

You’ll deliver engaging technical training, coach associates through practical projects and help them develop the skills they need for client placements.

Working closely with the Head of Training and the wider Academy team, you’ll also create and improve curriculum content, assess progress and adapt your delivery to support people with different levels of experience and learning needs.

This role would suit someone who enjoys making complex concepts accessible, takes a practical approach to teaching and wants to have a direct impact on people’s careers.

What you’ll be doing

Technical training and coaching

  • Deliver technical training, workshops and coaching sessions across our Academy programmes.
  • Bring learning to life through practical exercises, projects and examples that reflect how technology is used in the workplace.
  • Guide associates through technical challenges, helping them develop their problem-solving skills, independence and confidence.
  • Create an inclusive learning environment, adapting your approach to different backgrounds, abilities and learning needs.
  • Reinforce the communication, teamwork and professional skills associates need to contribute effectively in client teams.

Curriculum and content development

  • Work with the Head of Training to develop and maintain curriculum content, technical frameworks, assessments and learning resources.
  • Keep training relevant to industry practice, emerging technologies and the skills our clients need.
  • Collaborate with other trainers and specialist contractors to maintain consistent delivery and share effective teaching approaches.
  • Use feedback from associates, colleagues and client stakeholders to identify improvements and resolve issues with content or delivery.

Associate development and programme quality

  • Assess assignments and project work, providing clear, constructive feedback that helps associates understand their strengths and development areas.
  • Monitor progress and provide targeted coaching where associates need additional support.
  • Maintain accurate records of learning progress, assessments and feedback, keeping the wider Academy team informed of any concerns.
  • Work with colleagues across training, engagement and commercial teams to support associates’ preparation for client placements.
  • Participate in teaching observations and development activities, using feedback to improve your own practice.
  • Contribute to wider Academy projects and attraction activities, including open days, information sessions and workshops for prospective associates and clients.

Requirements

What we’re looking for

  • At least three years’ experience in a technical or training/coaching role.
  • Strong expertise in a relevant area of technology, with the ability to connect technical concepts to practical workplace applications.
  • Experience delivering training, coaching or mentoring, with a clear interest in helping others develop.
  • Excellent presentation and communication skills, including the ability to explain complex topics clearly and provide useful written feedback.
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to balance programme delivery, preparation, assessment and individual learner support.
  • Experience working with people from diverse backgrounds and adapting your approach to different needs.
  • The ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative training team.
  • A commitment to keeping your technical knowledge current and continuously improving the learning experience.

It would also be useful to have

  • A recognised teaching qualification, such as AET, CET, PGCE or an equivalent.
  • Experience delivering technology bootcamps, early-career training or Hire, Train, Deploy programmes.
  • Practical experience working in a commercial technology environment.
  • Knowledge of AI and how it is being applied across organisations.
  • Experience using learning management systems or digital platforms to deliver training and track progress.
  • Experience developing technical curriculum content, practical projects or assessments.

Benefits

Why join La Fosse Academy?

  • Help people build the skills, confidence and experience to begin or develop their careers in technology.
  • Influence the content and delivery of our training programmes, with the opportunity to bring your ideas and expertise into the curriculum.
  • Continue developing your own skills through training, coaching, mentoring and collaboration with experienced colleagues.
  • Be part of La Fosse’s employee-owned business and a wider group connected to the technology industry and the skills employers need.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and value the different experiences and perspectives they bring. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.

If you enjoy sharing your technical expertise and helping people turn their potential into practical skills, we’d love to hear from you.

Benefits

  • 🌴 Annual Leave: Enjoy up to 30 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays, your birthday off, and a Christmas closure period.
  • 🏙️ Hybrid Working Model: We work 3-4 days a week from our London office, with 2 weeks per year to work from anywhere, whether that’s by the beach, in the countryside, or closer to family.
  • 🎿 Annual Company Ski Trip: Hit the slopes with the team, our all-company ski trip is open to everyone.
  • 💆 Wellness Perks: We subsidise your gym membership to help you stay active and energised, and offer weekly in-office massages for a midweek recharge.
  • 🧠 Mental Health Support: Access to professional support and resources to help you prioritise your wellbeing.
  • 👶 Enhanced Maternity Pay: We provide enhanced maternity packages to support you through life’s important milestones.
  • 🎉 Incentives & Socials: Regular team socials, performance incentives, and rewards to celebrate your success.
  • 🦷 Private Health & Dental Discounts: Take advantage of discounted private healthcare and dental plans, because your health matters.

At La Fosse, we believe diverse teams create better outcomes. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. If this role excites you but you don’t tick every box, we still encourage you to apply!

description:
**Sustainability & Transformation Lead** (Contract)


Duration: 6 Months (Possibility for extension)

Location: London/Hybrid (4 days per week on site)

Rate: A highly competitive Umbrella Day Rate is available for suitable candidates


Role Overview


The successful candidate will report within the Sustainability Hub and will serve as the senior coordination and delivery lead for global sustainability regulatory programmes.

This role demands the ability to translate evolving regulatory requirements into scalable operating models, effective governance frameworks, robust controls, and high-quality disclosures across both enterprise and legal entity reporting.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute the firm's global sustainability regulatory strategy, ensuring alignment between enterprise sustainability objectives, regulatory requirements, and legal entity obligations.
  • Provide subject matter expertise and regulatory insight on sustainability and climate-related developments, assessing impacts, and advising senior management on emerging risks, opportunities, and priorities for implementation.
  • Translate regulatory requirements into actionable implementation strategies, governance frameworks, operating model enhancements, disclosure requirements, and delivery roadmaps.
  • Maintain a proactive view of regulatory changes, supervisory expectations, industry developments, and peer practises to inform strategic decision-making and enterprise prioritisation.
  • Coordinate the implementation of sustainability regulatory requirements across global and legal entity reporting obligations, ensuring a seamless transition from regulatory interpretation to implementation, disclosure readiness, and integration into business-as-usual processes.
  • Manage sustainability regulatory initiatives, ensuring accountability, effective prioritisation, timely delivery, and resolution of execution risks.
  • Foster cross-functional alignment among Sustainability, Risk, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Corporate Functions, and regional stakeholders to ensure coordinated execution.
  • Maintain traceability of regulatory requirements, documentation of implementation processes, and disclosure inventories to support transparency and audit readiness.
  • Oversee sustainability and climate-related disclosures across enterprise and legal entity reporting, ensuring compliance and alignment with regulatory expectations.
  • Enhance the firm's disclosure readiness through robust documentation standards, evidencing frameworks, controls, and assurance support mechanisms.
  • Collaborate with Finance, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Internal Audit to integrate sustainability regulatory requirements within the firm's governance and control environment.
  • Drive continuous improvements in reporting capabilities, controls, and processes to enhance efficiency and regulatory resilience.
  • Design and oversee the sustainability regulatory governance framework, including steering forums, governance engagement, escalation protocols, and reporting to the Board and Committees.
  • Establish and maintain a scalable global operating model that balances enterprise-wide consistency with jurisdictional and legal entity-specific regulatory requirements.
  • Enhance governance, accountability, and control initiatives to ensure effective ownership, monitoring, and execution of regulatory obligations across the organisation.
  • Manage, coach, and develop sustainability regulatory professionals, fostering a high-performing team environment and building organisational capability.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior executives and governance forums, influencing strategic decisions and aligning on sustainability regulatory priorities.
  • Represent the Sustainability Hub in interactions with internal governance forums, auditors, regulators, industry groups, investors, and other key stakeholders.


Skills & Experience:

  • Significant experience in sustainability regulation, sustainable finance, ESG reporting, risk management, finance, or related disciplines.
  • Deep expertise in global sustainability and climate-related regulatory frameworks, including CSRD, EU Taxonomy, ISSB, SEC climate-related requirements, CRR3, CRD VI, and Pillar 3 ESG reporting.
  • Proven track record in leading complex regulatory transformation programmes across multiple jurisdictions and corporate functions.
  • Strong experience in designing governance frameworks, operating models, disclosure processes, and assurance-ready reporting environments.

title: Specialist Engineer Strategy
description:
• Monday to Friday | West Perth Office with regular site travel
  • Performance, Retention and Profit Share Bonuses
  • Private health cover contribution for employees and immediate family
  • 18 Weeks paid Parental Leave for primary caregivers

Our vision:

As a leading iron ore producer, Hancock Iron Ore is helping secure the resources, jobs and prosperity that underpin the nation’s future. Guided by our vision to be the best mining company for Australia, we measure success not only by what we produce, but by the difference we make. We value creating opportunities, helping build regional and remote areas, and supporting Australian businesses by unlocking potential wherever it exists. Being 'For Australia' means delivering lasting benefits for today and for generations to come.

About the role:

We are seeking experienced Specialist Strategy Engineers to join our Asset Management team and play a critical role in shaping the long-term reliability, performance and sustainability of our fixed plant assets across our operations. Reporting to the Superintendent Fixed Plant Strategy, you will be responsible for providing specialist engineering expertise to improve our long-term asset performance, reduce risk and maximise equipment availability across critical fixed plant infrastructure. These positions are on a Monday-Friday roster, based at our West Perth office with regular travel to site.

We currently have three positions available, each specialising in one of the following asset classes:

  • Balance Machines
  • Rotating Equipment

These positions offer the opportunity to influence strategic asset decisions through maintenance strategy optimisation, defect elimination programs, reliability improvement initiatives and long-term asset planning. You will leverage equipment performance data, condition monitoring insights and engineering analysis to develop practical solutions that improve reliability, extend asset life and support operational excellence.

Duties:

  • Develop and maintain long-term asset strategies and Asset Management Plans for critical fixed plant assets
  • Lead reliability improvement and defect elimination initiatives, including the investigation and resolution of significant asset performance issues and Root Cause Analysis outcomes
  • Review and optimise maintenance tactics, asset strategies and master data to improve equipment performance, reliability and lifecycle value.
  • Deliver risk-based recommendations to support refurbishment, replacement and major maintenance planning activities
  • Support the design, maintainability and operability review of sustaining capital and infrastructure projects
  • Provide technical coaching and guidance to site-based Reliability Engineers, supporting capability development and knowledge sharing
  • Collaborate with Operations, Maintenance, Planning, Commercial, Supply and Engineering teams to deliver consistent reliability outcomes across sites
  • Engage with OEMs, vendors and specialist contractors to resolve chronic equipment issues and implement sustainable improvements
  • Ensure compliance with Asset Management standards, reliability engineering frameworks, governance requirements and engineering best practice

Skills and Experience:

  • Tertiary qualification in Mechanical Engineering or a related technical discipline
  • Extensive experience in reliability engineering, asset management, maintenance engineering or fixed plant engineering within the mining industry
  • Proven track record delivering reliability improvements, defect elimination programs and maintenance strategy optimisation
  • Strong knowledge of fixed plant assets, maintenance strategies, reliability methodologies and lifecycle asset management principles
  • Advanced knowledge of maintenance management systems, asset master data and reliability engineering tools such as RCM, FMEA and PM Optimisation

Success in this role requires a proactive and technically capable Mechanical Engineers, with strong foundations in reliability engineering and asset management. You will combine strategic thinking, analytical problem-solving and stakeholder engagement skills to solve complex equipment challenges, drive continuous improvement initiatives and deliver sustainable asset performance outcomes. Working collaboratively across the business, you will influence stakeholders, provide expert technical guidance and translate data-driven insights into practical solutions that create long-term operational value.

About Hancock Iron Ore

Hancock Iron Ore has a portfolio of world-class iron ore operations located in West Australia’s Pilbara region, with a strong history of delivering reliable products for our customers in key international markets. We have four operating mines: Roy Hill, Miralga Creek, Sanjiv Ridge, and McPhee Creek, plus a range of exciting development opportunities.
We deliver more than 70 million tonnes of ore each year through our own two-berth port facility at Stanley Point and the multi-user Utah Point in Port Hedland, providing the materials needed to foster global economic growth and development. Leveraging established infrastructure, including our processing plant and 344km independently owned and operated heavy haul railway, our operation oversees each moment from when ore is mined through to when it is shipped.

Located in the heart of West Perth, our headquarters offers a contemporary and collaborative workplace designed to support productivity, wellbeing and connection. From our popular on-site café, serving fresh breakfast and lunch options alongside barista-made coffee, to modern workspaces, rooftop terraces and end-of-trip facilities for active commuters, we've created an environment that combines great facilities with a workplace culture that helps our people thrive.

Hancock Iron Ore is an Equal Opportunity Employer and encourages Indigenous Australians, Veteran personnel and females to apply. We are a fair, diverse and welcoming workplace. We are proud of our relationships with our Traditional Owners and value the difference these partnerships make to the success of the project and to the lives of the people on whose land we operate.

Application Information

To be eligible to apply for this role you must be legally permitted to work permanently in Australia.

Job Description: National Railroad Safety Services, Inc. (NRSS) is seeking a Contractor in Charge (CIC) responsible for overseeing construction, maintenance, and safety compliance for freight railroads, transit systems, state DOTs, and rail industry partners.

title: Group Lead Product Manager
description:
About us

We’re the team behind digital retailer Very.

Our purpose, helping families get more out of life, powers everything we do.

And we want our people to get more out of life too! If you’re high-performing, ambitious and make the most of every opportunity, we want to hear from you. About the role

The moments when a customer joins Very, completes a purchase or manages their account have a huge influence on their overall experience with us.

We’re looking for a Group Lead Product Manager to define the future of these journeys across our app and website. You’ll own the vision and strategy for onboarding, checkout and My Account, helping us make every interaction clearer, easier and more valuable for our customers.

This is a senior product leadership opportunity with the scope to influence customer outcomes, conversion and revenue. You’ll bring several teams together behind a shared direction and ensure investment is focused on the most valuable problems to solve.

You will:

  • Set the vision, strategy and measurable outcomes for onboarding, checkout and My Account.
  • Lead, coach and develop Product Leaders
  • Turn customer research, behavioural insight and commercial data into clear product priorities.
  • Build experimentation, optimisation and learning into how teams make decisions.
  • Explore practical uses of AI that reduce customer effort and improve digital experiences.
  • Bring Product, Technology, UX, Analytics, Commercial and Trading teams together around shared outcomes.
  • Build compelling investment cases and represent the portfolio in senior leadership discussions.

About you

We’re looking for someone who can combine strategic product thinking with strong people leadership and commercial judgement.

You’ll ideally bring:

  • Significant product leadership experience gained in a large ecommerce or digital business.
  • Experience leading and developing Product owners
  • A strong record of defining product strategy and delivering measurable customer and commercial outcomes.
  • Deep knowledge of digital customer journeys, conversion and ecommerce performance.
  • Experience using experimentation, optimisation, personalisation and analytics to guide investment decisions.
  • An informed, practical understanding of how AI can improve ecommerce, customer experience or product development.
  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders and create alignment across multiple teams.

Some of our benefits

Please note that the talent acquisition team are managing this vacancy directly, and if successful in securing this role, you will be required to undertake a credit, CIFAS, Right to Work checks and if a specific requirement of your role a DBS (criminal records) check. Should your application progress we require you to let the team know if there is anything you need to disclose in relation to any of these checks prior to them being undertaken, including any unspent criminal convictions.

If it feels like we’re a good match, we’ll share your CV with the hiring manager to review. Our interview process is tailored to each role and can be in-person or held remotely.

1st stage - A 30-45 minute video call with the hiring team to discuss your skills and relevant experience. This is a great opportunity to find out more about the role and to ask any questions you may have.

2nd stage - A one-hour formal face-to-face interview where you can expect a task and both competency/technical skills based questions.

If you'd like to know more about our interviews, you can find out here.

Diversity, inclusion and equal opportunities

We’re building a culture of everyday inclusion, and welcome applications from anyone who believes they can do the job. We don’t discriminate based on age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

We want our recruitment process to be accessible to everyone. If you need reasonable adjustments to apply, interview, or perform a role, let us know via talentacquisition@theverygroup.com. We’ll be happy to support you.

We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Committed Employer and have nine brilliant colleague networks - including DAWN (Disability Awareness at Very) and Think (Neurodiversity at Very) - that are helping us make Very an even more inclusive place to work.

title: Fire Engineer
description:
Job Title: Fire Engineer
Location: National (will involve travel)
Salary: >£70,000 + Package


We are pleased to be working with this market leader in Passive Fire Protection who deliver trusted, high-quality fire protection services across the healthcare, commercial, residential, education, student accommodation, industrial, and infrastructure sectors. They pride themselves on getting it right first time, maintaining long-standing client relationships, and delivering work to the highest standards.


What You'll Do

Fire Engineering and Design;

  • Prepare fire strategies in accordance with UK Building Regulations, ADB, BS 9999, BS 9991, BS 7974 and associated guidance.
  • Prepare retrospective fire strategies for existing buildings, including HRBs, using available records, site inspection evidence and relevant current guidance.
  • Support external wall fire assessments and facade remediation projects, including review of facade build-ups, cavity barriers, fire stopping, insulation, membranes, cladding systems and interfaces.
  • Produce fire engineering calculations and technical assessments to support design solutions.
  • Undertake fire risk assessments and provide recommendations for existing and new buildings.
  • Assist with smoke control, means of escape, structural fire engineering and passive fire protection assessments.
  • Review active fire protection systems including fire detection, suppression and smoke management systems.
  • Support the integration of fire safety into modern methods of construction (MMC), sustainable developments and digital design environments.
  • Contribute to BIM coordination and ensure fire safety information is accurately incorporated into project models and documentation.
  • Collaborate with architectural, structural and MEP disciplines to deliver coordinated fire safety solutions.


Project Delivery and Risk Management;

  • Deliver allocated fire engineering projects safely, efficiently and within agreed programme and budget.
  • Prepare technical reports, specifications and supporting documentation to company quality standards.
  • Carry out site and quality assurance (QA) inspections to verify fire safety measures, including facade remediation works, cavity barriers, fire stopping and other passive fire protection, against approved designs and manufacturer's or system requirements.
  • Review contractor submissions, drawings and product information relating to fire safety systems.
  • Support construction-stage fire assurance activities and identify deviations from approved fire strategies.
  • Support post-occupancy reviews and continuous improvement initiatives where required.


Compliance and Regulatory Engagement;

  • Ensure compliance with the Building Safety Act, Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order, Building Regulations and relevant British Standards.
  • Assist with Building Control consultations and engagement with Fire and Rescue Services.
  • Support HRB projects under the Building Safety Act and Building Safety Regulator regime, including the preparation and review of Building Safety Case documentation and Golden Thread information.
  • Maintain awareness of changes to legislation, Approved Documents and industry best practice.
  • Participate in internal technical reviews and quality assurance processes.

Innovation, Knowledge Leadership and Work Winning;

  • Contribute to the development of technical guidance notes, standard details and engineering templates.
  • Support innovation in digital engineering, fire modelling and sustainable fire safety design.
  • Share knowledge and lessons learned across the wider engineering team.
  • Maintain awareness of emerging fire engineering technologies, standards and research.


What You'll Bring

  • Degree in Fire Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
  • Experience working within fire engineering or fire safety consultancy.
  • Experience working on existing buildings and HRBs, including retrospective fire strategies, facade remediation and construction-stage QA inspections.
  • Understanding of UK Building Regulations and fire safety legislation.
  • Ability to manage workload across multiple projects.
  • Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel where required.

title: Security Specialist/HARPS Guard I - PT On Call Floater hours
description:
Position: PART-TIME PT with Floater hours


SCHEDULE: Saturday & Sunday, 6am - 6 pm every other weekend with on-call floater hours


Specific Tasks. The following tasks are general duties for the HARPS personnel. Contracting Personnel (CP) providing service at JBSA-Lackland and Randolph, AFB shall perform the following tasks below;

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS: • Monitor all electromagnetic door locks, door contact switches, duress alarms and answer all telephone calls within the HARPS/Information Desk Control Area. This area is defined as the Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) room, and the adjacent administrative area commonly referred to as the Information Desk. • Personnel will monitor the Identipass, Genetech, and Premisys access control systems. • Initial training for these systems will be provided by a company representative of which the system is being provided by. The contractor will then be responsible to train any new CP thereafter. • The government will phase out any of the systems that will eventually no longer be in use. • Operate, observe and evaluate CCTVs within the HARPS/Information Desk Control Area. • Use the Government provided radio system to notify the Facility Management staff and/or the base installation Security Forces on any alarm or police response situations. • Monitor operations and status of overall security network for the MTF from the centralized console. • Operate HARPS/Information Desk intercom system master station at the console to communicate with entry/exit points or incident locations. • Utilize overhead paging system to notify personnel of emergency codes and alarms. Communicate all information in a clear and concise manner. • Operate video recorder and playback at the request of Facility Management personnel. • Maintain security log and activate control devices for interior and exterior doors. • Receive transfer calls from designated wing agencies and take messages or forward calls to appropriate agencies. • Report and initiate an action report log on any emergency situation and provide comprehensive information to responding agencies and Facility Management staff when appropriate. • Maintain up to date roster of on-call and emergency contact personnel for required areas. • The CP report to an appropriate authority (DCS Supervisors, Security Forces, and Facility Managers) any information or circumstances, which may pose a threat to the security of DoD personnel, contractor personnel, resources, and classified or unclassified defense information. • Maintain Chronology of Events, Access Control logs and Alarm Reports at all times. Event logs will be documented in a professional manner utilizing appropriate grammar and punctuation and include all pertinent information covering the parameters of “Who, What, When, and Where.” Event logs will be sent to Facility Management on a daily basis no later than 0800 hrs. These documents are for official use only. • CP shall perform and document physical checks of assigned buildings, rooms and areas when electronic systems are degraded. This includes manual fire watch procedures when fire alarm systems are down and checks of controlled areas such as pharmacies when Intrution Detection Systems (IDS) are degraded. • Act as the information focal point for all medical groups' personnel, patients and visitors on all resource protection activities and the liaison on these issues to the facility management office.


Qualifications.

  1. Have 12 months of experience as an alarm monitor or dispatcher, either in the military or civilian sector, within the last 3 years.
  2. Skills and Knowledge. Must be able to use, at minimum, Access Control System, Genetech, and Microsoft Programs such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  3. Shall be capable of sitting for an extended period of time during the course of their 8-hour shift, but are able to get up and move about within the area. CP shall be capable of bending, reaching, and lifting a minimum of 30 pounds to move and retrieve records or equipment, and may require prolonged walking and or standing.
  4. Personnel must be able to communicate in a clear and concise manner and demonstrate a calm demeanor during high-stress situations

title: Senior Risk Data Scientist
description:
Senior Risk Data Scientist

Remote (London) | £80,000 - £85,000 + Benefits

This is an opportunity to join an innovative data-driven business that is transforming how risk is assessed and managed within the payments ecosystem. title: Parts Coordinator
description:
Job Description: Parts Coordinator


The Parts Coordinator is responsible for the daily ordering and processing of all vehicle repair parts requirements. The Parts Coordinator must ensure correct parts on-hand when needed for technicians for production flow and to meet repair timeframes. They must actively participate in the communication and Repair Order processing needs of the Estimators.

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Work Location: Full Time Hourly

Job Responsibilities:

  • Check-in all received parts as they arrive: sort, mirror-match to the Repair Order and vehicle, label and distribute.
  • Process returns immediately and receive credit for incorrect or damaged parts, including document & reconcile for credit: “Damaged Delivered Parts,” handle parts returns processing: “Return Parts to Credit Invoice,” and maintain record system for “Returned Parts” tracking, including core charges.
  • Responsible for keeping a 5S clean & organized delivery area, returns no more than 1 week old, and parts cart, with current CCC parts list attached to it.
  • Ensure all parts and sublet lines are posted in CCC real time and accurately, and all materials billed have an invoice.
  • Post invoices / credits same day if no line on estimate draft the invoice.
  • Maintain the Daily “Parts Owed” List by reviewing “Scheduled In” Repair Orders for Part’s Requirements
  • Ensure daily production schedule with parts ETA and any sublet items that are or need to be scheduled.
  • Requests sublet vendor work as needed and ensures invoices are received and posted to the RO.
  • Monitor CCC to determine outstanding parts to prioritize and follow up on, adding notes for daily production meeting updates.
  • Assist Estimators as needed with ordering required parts and any supplemental parts during work in process vehicles utilizing the parts ordering system. Ensure availability and accurate parts orders the first time for efficiency.
  • Assist and be a team player in other areas as needed or requested for shop efficiency and productivity. These requests could include picking up parts, driving customers, washing vehicles for delivery, and minor buffing and polishing of vehicles.

Key Performance Metrics

  • Proper Parts Posting for increased profitability.
  • Parts Return and Credits, zero over 30 days.

Skills/Qualifications:

  • Collision University Training required in first 6 months of employment.


Behavioral Excellence Required:

  • Perform all assigned responsibilities according to the Company Standard Operating Procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized work area always, adhering to 5S organization.
  • Participate in training programs as required to maintain the technical and professional skills and techniques necessary for this position.
  • Adheres to the company’s non-disclosure and confidentiality policies concerning customer information.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work in both office and automotive repair shop environments.
  • Ability to stand and walk frequently throughout the workday while locating, receiving, distributing, and inventorying parts.
  • Ability to move throughout the facility, including production, paint, receiving, storage, and parking areas.
  • Ability to frequently bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, reach, and climb as necessary to retrieve, organize, and store parts and materials.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 pounds occasionally and up to 25 pounds frequently; heavier items may require assistance or mechanical equipment.
  • Ability to load, unload, sort, and organize parts, supplies, and materials in a safe and efficient manner.
  • Ability to use hands and fingers for frequent handling, grasping, sorting, labeling, packaging, and inventory management activities.
  • Ability to operate computers, inventory management systems, scanners, and other office equipment for extended periods.
  • Ability to visually inspect parts for accuracy, damage, defects, and proper fitment, including close and distance vision.
  • Ability to compare part numbers, repair orders, invoices, and other documentation with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with technicians, estimators, vendors, customers, and coworkers in person, by telephone, and electronically.
  • Ability to safely navigate around moving vehicles, equipment, tools, and active repair operations.
  • Ability to tolerate exposure to noise, dust, fumes, varying temperatures, and other conditions commonly found in a collision repair environment while utilizing required personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Ability to maintain organization and accuracy while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Ability to operate a motor vehicle and maintain a valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record, if required to pick up, deliver, or move parts and vehicles.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.
